sources.note: The proposed first task of a Verify Session: reconstruct a single 'Candidate KnowledgeOS Theory' target from the whole relevant corpus (book + mathematical artifacts + architecture + historical evidence, each with a distinct authority role) via a Theory Corpus Map inventory table, before any substantive verification begins.

rows.anchor: **The Candidate KnowledgeOS Mathematical Theory (CKT)** ... but the book is not automatically the authoritative mathematical source.
rows.statement: Defines the verification target as a single central object, the Candidate KnowledgeOS Mathematical Theory (CKT), which must first be reconstructed from the ENTIRE relevant corpus (book, mathematical artifacts, architecture artifacts, historical/research evidence) rather than treating the book as automatically authoritative -- 'we could end up proving that the book is internally consistent while the underlying KnowledgeOS theory is wrong.'

rows.anchor: Book says X. but: Original derivation actually establishes only Y. That becomes a verification finding.
rows.statement: Warns that the book (Edition 2) may silently strengthen or misstate what an original mathematical artifact actually establishes, e.g. book claiming A<=>B when the original derivation only supports A=>B -- such a divergence itself becomes a verification finding, with the rule that 'the book strengthened the theory' rather than forcing the mathematics to fit the book.

rows.anchor: architecture is evidence, not mathematical authority. ... it must never reason backward: 'The software does X, therefore the mathematical theory says X.' Instead: Theory -> Architecture -> Implementation is the direction of verification.
rows.statement: Establishes that architecture/implementation artifacts are evidence for conformance, never mathematical authority for the theory itself; verification must run Theory->Architecture->Implementation and never infer theoretical claims backward from what the software happens to do.

rows.anchor: Historical artifacts establish: What was actually proposed, derived, observed or decided. They do not establish mathematical truth merely because something was recorded. ... Historical truth separate from Mathematical truth.
rows.statement: Keeps historical truth (what was actually proposed/derived/recorded) strictly separate from mathematical truth (whether a proposition is actually valid); historical evidence establishes provenance, never mathematical correctness by mere fact of being recorded.

rows.anchor: ## Phase V0 — Theory Inventory ... Produce a Theory Corpus Map: | ID | Artifact | Contains | Authority role |
rows.statement: Proposes Phase V0 (Theory Inventory) as the Verify Session's first task: locate every place the candidate theory exists and produce a Theory Corpus Map table (ID, artifact, contents, authority role e.g. candidate/derived-representation/implementation-evidence/execution-evidence) before attempting any substantive verification.

rows.anchor: This map records where the Candidate KnowledgeOS Theory (CKT) exists and what role each artifact plays. It reconciles nothing. Disagreements are recorded in §5.
rows.statement: Defines the V0 map's scope and non-goal: it records where the Candidate KnowledgeOS Theory exists and each artifact's role/authority, explicitly reconciling nothing -- disagreements are only recorded, never adjudicated.

rows.anchor: STRATUM 1 RAW RESEARCH RECORD ... STRATUM 2 CONSOLIDATED CANDIDATE MODEL ... STRATUM 3 CONSTITUTIONAL / GOVERNANCE LAYER ... STRATUM 4 EXPOSITION
rows.statement: Identifies four authority strata for the Candidate KnowledgeOS Theory: raw research record (non-authoritative, ~460+163+102 files), consolidated candidate model (authorized as canonical model, not verified theory), constitutional/governance layer (accepted, prose-normative, essentially math-free), and exposition (derived representation, forbidden from exceeding its sources) -- plus separate Witnesses and Prior-Verification categories.

rows.anchor: the corpus contains no axiom register (AX-*: zero hits corpus-wide), no unified transition function (~25 distinct right-hand sides for K_{t+1}), and — despite the folder name — no measure theory (deferred by recorded decision on day 1 ... and never resumed; sigma-algebra appears once in 460 files, a
rows.statement: Grep-verified absence findings with direct consequence for the verification programme: zero axiom-register hits corpus-wide, roughly 25 mutually distinct proposed right-hand sides for the K_{t+1} transition function with none ratified, and no measure theory anywhere in the phase_measure_theory folder despite its name (measure theory was deferred on day 1 and never resumed; sigma-algebra appears exactly once, as a bullet point).

rows.anchor: T-001 | canonical-architecture-v0.2.md | ... AUTHORIZED canonical model (GN-19); md5-pinned | PRIMARY L1 target — the single most authoritative statement of the CKT
rows.statement: Identifies T-001 (the ratified canonical-architecture-v0.2, GN-19, md5-pinned) as the single most authoritative statement of the Candidate KnowledgeOS Theory and the primary Level-1 verification target.

rows.anchor: T-013 | # Step 158…205 series ... 189 formal epistemic state (3 state machines) · 197 conservation laws · 198 composition · 199 uncertainty/probability · 200 coherence test · 203 state-space decomposition · 204 transition algebra · 205 aggregate derivation ... filename hygiene hazard (no .md, # and
rows.statement: Explicitly catalogs this batch's own Step 189-205 sequence (T-013) as 'the most recent formal statements' with Steps 203-205 called 'the closest to a transition calculus', while flagging a filename hygiene hazard (no .md extension, '#' and spaces in names) that any scripted pass over the folder must handle.

lineage_claims.quote: 189 formal epistemic state (3 state machines) · 197 conservation laws · 198 composition · 199 uncertainty/probability · 200 coherence test · 203 state-space decomposition · 204 transition algebra · 205 aggregate derivation

rows.anchor: T-020 | mathematical-verification-report.md ... the formal-object layer is signatures without constructions — eta, Learn, ladder transition calculus, policy-version calculus, r<->P typing map UNDER-SPECIFIED ... This programme's L1 must treat MV-F verdicts as claims to re-verify, not as truth
rows.statement: Records the prior independent mathematical-verification report's finding that the formal-object layer consists of 'signatures without constructions' (several named calculi under-specified), explicitly instructing the new verification programme to treat those prior MV-F verdicts as claims to re-verify, never as established truth.

rows.anchor: T-024 ... verdict DEFER; 13 apparent contradictions dissolved; 2 genuine tensions survive, both constitutional (ziran vs INV-KOS-IDENTITY-001; S1-F016+ziran composition)
rows.statement: Records a prior independent kernel review's DEFER verdict, which dissolved thirteen apparent contradictions but left two genuine, undisposed constitutional tensions (a Daoist ziran attack against INV-KOS-IDENTITY-001, and a composition of S1-F016+ziran against it) as standing candidate counterexample material.

rows.anchor: T-025 ... measure-theory cascade (9 docs ...): v0.1 proposal → 5 refutations (incl. 'six category errors') → resolution ('formalisms are regimes') → meta-refutation of the resolution ... Load-bearing negative result.
rows.statement: Records the corpus's own measure-theory cascade as a load-bearing negative result: an initial proposal was refuted five times (including a 'six category errors' critique), the resulting 'formalisms are regimes' doctrine was itself attacked by a post-cutoff meta-refutation, and no disposition of that meta-refutation exists -- the verification programme must check whether the CKT still tacitly relies on structures this cascade rejected.

rows.anchor: T-040/T-041/T-042 ... Evidence level C — witnesses, never proofs (Mandate §13) ... the expressibility probe (Accepted AND Contest:Active has no single-state representation) ... re-derives the CSV-vs-verdict discrepancy
rows.statement: Catalogs three computational witnesses (a Zero reference implementation, a ladder/Decision-Contract reference implementation whose expressibility probe finds 'Accepted AND active Contest' has no single-state representation, and an independent re-implementation of the EXP-01 evidence-aggregation operators confirming a known CSV-vs-verdict discrepancy) -- all explicitly graded Evidence level C, witnesses never proofs.

rows.anchor: T-050 ... The constitutional invariants are not mathematical statements; L1 must decide per-invariant whether a formal counterpart exists in the CKT — a mapping that does not currently exist
rows.statement: Notes that the accepted eleven-law constitutional core and its INV-KOS-* invariant register are prose-normative, not mathematical statements, and that a mapping from each constitutional invariant to a formal mathematical counterpart in the Candidate Theory does not currently exist anywhere in the corpus.

rows.anchor: Standing formula (GN-10): 'architecturally coherent and substantially evidence-supported; formal synthesis and implementation conformance remain to be established' — NEVER 'validated'.
rows.statement: States the corpus's own standing governance formula (GN-10) for describing the theory's status: architecturally coherent and substantially evidence-supported, with formal synthesis and implementation conformance still to be established -- explicitly never described as 'validated'.

rows.anchor: the production-log findings (PF-1…9) already record that the ratified layer is in places a lossy compression of the raw mathematics, with disposition pending.
rows.statement: Flags that the canonical extraction cannot simply trust the authorized/ratified layer at face value, since production-log findings already record the ratified model as in places a lossy compression of richer raw-track mathematics, with disposition still pending -- requiring bidirectional checking against the raw track.

rows.anchor: D-01 ~25 mutually distinct right-hand sides for K_{t+1} (delta, T, T_K, Transition, Update, Revision, +DeltaK, F(...), I^K_t, Derive(...)) with no ratified canonical form
rows.statement: D-01: approximately 25 mutually distinct proposed right-hand sides for the core K_{t+1} transition function exist across 240 files referencing K_t, with no ratified canonical form -- the single most load-bearing unresolved mathematical disagreement in the corpus.

rows.anchor: D-02 K_t arity conflict: 10-tuple vs 5-tuple vs (D_I,V_I,R_I,C_I,P_I) vs book's K=(E,S,T,O,P,R,Pi,A) 8-tuple
rows.statement: D-02: at least four mutually incompatible arities/structures are proposed for the core knowledge-state tuple K_t (a 10-tuple, a 5-tuple, another 5-tuple, and the book's own 8-tuple), unreconciled.

rows.anchor: D-04 Z_t signature conflict: Zero(K_t,I_t,Q_t,C_t) vs (U_t,C_t,A_t,R_t) vs Zero(K_t,I_t)->Delta_t vs Zero(K_t,I_t,P_t,C_t) vs ratified Zero(K,EC) (FA-4)
rows.statement: D-04: at least five distinct signatures are proposed for the Zero function across the raw track and the ratified layer, unreconciled -- Zero as a function of state and various combinations of identity/quality/context/authority/policy, versus the ratified two-argument Zero(K,EC).

rows.anchor: D-05 DC(d) tuple arity: book states a six-tuple; source states seven-tuple <P,I,A,E,Q,T,O> ... D-06 Three competing consolidation candidates for 'the current theory' ... no artifact states their mutual relationship
rows.statement: D-05: the book's Decision Contract is stated as a six-tuple while its own cited source states a seven-tuple. D-06: three competing candidates all claim to be 'the current theory' (the authorized canonical-architecture-v0.2, the most recent Step 201/202 vocabulary freeze, and an earlier best-structured but superseded 'Complete Mathematical Model'), with no artifact ever stating their mutual relationship.

rows.anchor: D-08 Stale status artifact: book-edition-2/00-edition-2-index.md claims Part II pending; governance-notes ledger (GN-57…GN-68) records Part II complete/GREEN with acceptance review in flight
rows.statement: D-08: the Edition-2 index file claims Part II is still pending while the governance-notes master ledger (GN-57 through GN-68) records Part II as complete and GREEN with acceptance review in flight -- the index file is stale.

rows.anchor: D-10 Lossy-compression family: PF-1…PF-9 / AF-F-9 / AF-F-11 record that the ratified model compresses richer corpus math; disposition pending. ... D-11 EXP-01 register discrepancy (CSV vs verdict) — confirmed by independent re-execution
rows.statement: D-10: a family of production findings records the ratified model as a lossy compression of richer corpus mathematics, disposition pending. D-11: an EXP-01 CSV-vs-verdict register discrepancy has been independently confirmed by re-execution, corroborating an earlier governance finding (GN-27).

rows.anchor: Built from four parallel sweeps using exhaustive listing and grep-based formal-density scanning, with selective reading of high-density artifacts. ... this map does not claim full-text reading of the ~1,350-file corpus.
rows.statement: Discloses the map's own coverage limitation: built from listing plus grep-based scanning with selective reading, not full-text reading of the ~1,350-file corpus; absence claims (no axioms, no LaTeX, single sigma-algebra hit) are grep-verified and therefore strong, while content claims about individual sampled files are correct only at the level actually sampled.

rows.anchor: One sweep observed an instruction-like text block appended inside a read file's content ('You have exited plan mode…'); it was treated as untrusted data and ignored.
rows.statement: Records a process-safety observation: one sweep found an instruction-like text block appended inside a source file's content, which was correctly treated as untrusted data and ignored rather than acted upon.

rows.anchor: 1. Spine: T-001 ... + T-005 ... + T-061 ... 2. Mathematical flesh: T-006…T-015 ... 3. Statistical layer: T-014 + T-016 ... 4. Invariants: T-002 ... 5. Every disagreement D-01…D-12 enters the specification as recorded variance — not resolved.
rows.statement: States the five-point handoff plan to the next stage (V1, Candidate Theory Specification): anchor on the authorized/ratified spine plus the raw mathematical track plus the statistical layer tested against external anchors, use the invariant-map as the classification spine, and carry every one of the twelve recorded disagreements forward as unresolved variance rather than silently resolving any of them.

rows.anchor: EXPLICIT ... INFERRED ... RECONSTRUCTED ... UNDEFINED ... SIGNATURE-ONLY. Nothing here is repaired. Where the prior GN-46 audit judged completeness, that judgment is recorded as prior-audit claim — to be independently re-checked at Level 1, not assumed.
rows.statement: Defines the register's five-value tag vocabulary (EXPLICIT, INFERRED, RECONSTRUCTED, UNDEFINED, SIGNATURE-ONLY) and its cardinal discipline: nothing is repaired here, and even a prior audit's completeness judgment is recorded only as a claim to be independently re-verified, never assumed.

rows.anchor: EC = eta(G, IdealState) ... eta: SIGNATURE-ONLY — no construction; totality ASSUMED (OQ-1) ... 'NO — signature only'; computability NOT ESTABLISHED
rows.statement: The ratified Epistemic Contract function EC=eta(G,IdealState) is graded SIGNATURE-ONLY -- no actual construction exists anywhere in the corpus, its totality is merely assumed (open question OQ-1), and computability was never established.

rows.anchor: EC structure ... source-final forms: (R,Gamma,A,V) 4-tuple, 9-tuple (025e), 8-tuple recap (025f) — source-internal inconsistency, recorded ... MV-F-4 (unregistered compression + 8-vs-9 inconsistency)
rows.statement: The Epistemic Contract's internal structure is recorded with three mutually inconsistent arities across the source material itself (a 4-tuple, a 9-tuple, and an 8-tuple recap), an internal inconsistency the register explicitly preserves rather than silently picking one.

rows.anchor: Evidence e ... EXPLICIT at tuple level; ~ (epistemic equivalence) UNDEFINED — by the source's own admission ... MV-F-22 (identity calculus missing)
rows.statement: Evidence is explicitly defined at the tuple level, but the epistemic-equivalence relation '~' it depends on is undefined by the source's own admission, connecting to the still-missing 'identity calculus' (MV-F-22).

rows.anchor: Aggregation operators A1–A4 ... BAYES undefined on {0,1} jointly; WM undefined on empty-set (MV-F-18); operator selection OPEN (OQ-3)
rows.statement: The four ratified evidence-aggregation operators (SATURATING, BAYES-like, MAX, WM) have explicit formulas but known edge-case gaps (BAYES undefined when evidence values are jointly 0 and 1; WM undefined on an empty evidence set), and which operator to select in a given case remains an open question.

rows.anchor: K_t (KnowledgeState) ... state equality UNDEFINED ... kernel membership at object level [U] (OQ-2)
rows.statement: The core KnowledgeState K_t has explicit contents (eight primitives) but no definition of state equality anywhere, and whether it counts as kernel-level remains an open question at the object level.

rows.anchor: AcceptancePolicy ... in-force uniqueness under multiple authorities NOT ESTABLISHED (MV-F-7); genesis base case ABSENT (MV-F-8)
rows.statement: AcceptancePolicy's role is explicit, but its uniqueness under multiple authorities is not established and its genesis base case (how the very first in-force policy came to exist) is entirely absent from the corpus.

rows.anchor: Zero(K, EC) = Z_t ... not a metric (directed, purpose-relative, structured) ... status-set closure NOT ESTABLISHED ... 𝒮 not closed (MV-F-3)
rows.statement: The ratified Zero(K,EC) gap function is explicitly defined at the vector level and explicitly not a metric (directed, purpose-relative, structured), but its status-set closure was never established -- the satisfaction set S is not closed (MV-F-3).

rows.anchor: Satisfaction set 𝒮 | nine named values ... I-9's 'four-way' is the ratified compression ... MV-F-2 (I-9's 'four-way' INVALID as source description); PF-1 load-bearing losses {Insufficient, Stale, Prohibited}
rows.statement: The satisfaction set has nine named source values, but the ratified invariant I-9 compresses this to a 'four-way' distinction that is flagged as an INVALID description of the actual source (MV-F-2), with three named values (Insufficient, Stale, Prohibited) recorded as load-bearing losses in that compression.

rows.anchor: Decision selector ... source forms (K,G,D,C,P)->d, S(K,G,D,M,C), Sarathi(K,D,DecisionModel) — unratified (PF-8) ... MV-F-6: ratified flow edge PROPOSAL -> DECISION under DC(d) not type-correct — nothing ratified produces d
rows.statement: The function that actually produces a decision d is never ratified (three competing source forms exist, all unratified per PF-8), and the ratified flow diagram's PROPOSAL->DECISION edge is not even type-correct -- nothing ratified in the corpus actually produces a decision (MV-F-6).

rows.anchor: Governance algebra ... only one row ratified; ⪰_C's partial-order axioms never stated or argued ... PF-9 CONFIRMED (I-11 presupposes uniqueness of in-force policy)
rows.statement: The governance precedence algebra (context-indexed authority precedence, applicability, conflict, resolution, escalation) has only one row ever ratified, and the partial-order axioms its own precedence relation would need were never stated or argued anywhere -- confirmed (PF-9) that invariant I-11 quietly presupposes the uniqueness of the in-force policy without that uniqueness being established.

rows.anchor: Learn | K_{t+1} = Learn(K_t, Obs, Events, Policies, Outcomes) | SIGNATURE-ONLY — uninterpreted function symbol | MV-F-11; no governed OQ flag (unlike eta)
rows.statement: The core knowledge-update function Learn (K_{t+1}=Learn(K_t,Obs,Events,Policies,Outcomes)) is entirely SIGNATURE-ONLY, an uninterpreted function symbol with no construction anywhere -- and unlike the similarly-uninterpreted eta, it does not even carry a governed open-question flag.

rows.anchor: To be merged from the three extraction sweeps: K_t/S_t tuple families and the ~25 transition forms (Q13/Q15/Q20, step-031, Steps 189/201–205) ... Recorded variance carried from V0 (not to be resolved here): D-01…D-05
rows.statement: Names this batch's own Step 189 and Steps 201-205 (already extracted earlier in this same batch, S1390/S1420-S1424) as raw-track material still pending merge into this register, explicitly carrying forward V0's disagreements D-01 through D-05 (transition-form and tuple-arity conflicts) as unresolved variance rather than adjudicating them here.

lineage_claims.quote: Recorded variance carried from V0 (not to be resolved here): D-01…D-05 (transition forms; K_t/S_t/Z_t/DC arities).

rows.anchor: STATED (explicitly labeled in source) · RULED (assumed by governance act) · REQUIRED-UNSTATED (needed for a derivation/definition to work, not stated ...) · ORACLE (assumption that an external capability exists). ... Entries marked REQUIRED-UNSTATED are my identification of a dependency, not corpus
rows.statement: Defines the assumption register's four-class vocabulary (STATED, RULED, REQUIRED-UNSTATED, ORACLE) and its discipline of clearly separating the verifier's own dependency-identification work (REQUIRED-UNSTATED) from actual corpus content.

rows.anchor: AS-R01 eta is total: EC = eta(G, IdealState) is defined for every (G, IdealState) | RULED (synthesis decision, revisitable)
rows.statement: The totality of eta (that EC is defined for every possible Goal/IdealState pair) is a ruled synthesis decision, not a proven mathematical fact, and is explicitly revisitable.

rows.anchor: AS-R03 Per-requirement evaluators exist (rules/statistics/authority as oracles; HumanAuthorization is not a computation) | ORACLE
rows.statement: Zero's computability is only 'relative to evaluators' -- the existence of per-requirement evaluators (including HumanAuthorization, explicitly not a computation) is treated as an oracle assumption, not something the theory itself constructs.

rows.anchor: AS-R06 Normalization (dedup/dependency collapse) precedes aggregation — I-5's claimed properties hold only under this pipeline assumption | STATED (as I-6) but its carrier ~ is UNDEFINED
rows.statement: Invariant I-5's duplicate-invariance property holds only under the I-6 pipeline-ordering assumption, but the epistemic-equivalence relation '~' that this pipeline assumption itself depends on remains undefined.

rows.anchor: AS-R07 Conditional independence where BAYES-like combination is applied | REQUIRED-UNSTATED at operator level ... GN-46 §7 numeric demo (0.80→0.985 inflation)
rows.statement: The BAYES-like aggregation operator requires conditional independence of the combined evidence, an assumption flagged narratively in the design doc but never actually tested by the operator itself; a prior numeric demonstration (GN-46 section 7) showed the resulting confidence inflating from 0.80 to 0.985 when this assumption fails.

rows.anchor: AS-R11 preceq_C is a partial order (reflexive/transitive/antisymmetric) | REQUIRED-UNSTATED — postulated, axioms never stated or argued
rows.statement: The context-indexed authority precedence relation is simply postulated to be a partial order; its reflexivity/transitivity/antisymmetry axioms were never actually stated or argued anywhere in the source.

assumptions.statement: the governance precedence relation preceq_C is a partial order

rows.anchor: AS-R13 Bounded action space 𝒜(K_t); selector-loop termination additionally needs a budget/deadline/termination policy that is not part of the ratified model | STATED (need named by source itself: 'termination algebra')
rows.statement: The Proposal selector loop's termination requires a budget/deadline/termination policy that the source itself names as needed ('termination algebra') but which is not actually part of the ratified model.

rows.anchor: AS-R14 State equality / evidence equivalence / frame equivalence / requirement identity exist — an identity calculus is presupposed by I-5, replay/determinism, and any Gamma<->rho_A identification | REQUIRED-UNSTATED (4 instances of one missing foundation)
rows.statement: A single missing foundational 'identity calculus' (state equality, evidence equivalence, frame equivalence, requirement identity) is presupposed in at least four separate places (invariant I-5, replay/determinism claims, and any Gamma-to-rho_A identification), making it one unstated assumption manifesting as four instances of the same gap.

assumptions.statement: state equality, evidence equivalence, frame equivalence, and requirement identity are all well-defined

rows.anchor: AS-R15 Epistemic status is not probability; no probability space is claimed; Pr(P|E) >= 0.95 is a policy example only | STATED (refusal)
rows.statement: The ratified layer explicitly refuses to claim a probability space for epistemic status -- any probability-threshold example (e.g. Pr(P|E)>=0.95) is stated to be illustrative policy example only, not a mathematical claim about the model itself.

rows.anchor: AS-R18 Learn and F are assumed to exist as functions (uninterpreted symbols) — every dynamic claim about K_{t+1} presupposes them | REQUIRED-UNSTATED (openness of eta is governed via OQ-1; Learn/F carry no analogous flag)
rows.statement: Every dynamic claim about how K_{t+1} evolves presupposes that Learn and F exist as functions, yet unlike eta (which is at least governed by an open question OQ-1), Learn and F carry no analogous governance flag despite being equally uninterpreted.

assumptions.statement: Learn and F exist as well-defined functions governing K_{t+1}

rows.anchor: AS-R19 The 8-primitive set is a candidate reduction, not proven minimal/complete/unique — any use of 'the kernel' as if minimal imports an unstated minimality assumption | STATED (as caveat)
rows.statement: The eight-primitive KnowledgeState decomposition is only a candidate reduction, never proven minimal, complete, or unique; any later use of 'the kernel' as if it were minimal silently imports this unstated minimality assumption.

rows.anchor: AS-R20 Zero's status set 𝒮 is closed (fixed membership) | REQUIRED-UNSTATED — source says 'initially I propose'; membership drifts (Missing, Failed)
rows.statement: The closedness of Zero's satisfaction-status set is a required-but-unstated assumption; the source itself only ever says 'initially I propose' the set, and its membership demonstrably drifts over time (Missing and Failed were added/used later).

assumptions.statement: Zero's satisfaction status set S has fixed, closed membership

rows.anchor: Checkpoint feed: every REQUIRED-UNSTATED row above is a candidate for report section E (hidden assumptions); AS-R09/R10/R11/R14/R18/R20 are simultaneously candidates for section C (load-bearing) risk ranking.
rows.statement: Routes every REQUIRED-UNSTATED assumption toward a future hidden-assumptions report section, additionally flagging six of them (AS-R09, R10, R11, R14, R18, R20) as simultaneously load-bearing risk-ranking candidates.

rows.anchor: Conditional-evidence 'v2-expanded' is not a revision: v2 = v1 byte-identical + a concatenated third document (the Kernel Problem file). Two halves of v2 disagree (K14 below). ... The SNF file contains two voices ... both retained with no supersession mark (K6).
rows.statement: Structural finding: a file labeled 'v2-expanded' is not actually a revision (it is v1 byte-identical plus a concatenated unrelated document whose content disagrees with v1), and the SNF measurement file contains two voices (a review and a critique that materially overrides it) retained side by side with no supersession mark.

rows.anchor: Belief is boxed as distinct (027 §27.1), then only ever used as Bayes-updated probability (027 §27.20; 082 §82.21–23), and finally banned from the kernel vocabulary by the KST extraction (lines 2422, 2604). No non-probabilistic definition of Belief exists anywhere. (K3)
rows.statement: K3: the term Belief is explicitly boxed as a distinct concept from probability, but is then only ever used in practice as Bayes-updated probability, and is finally banned outright from the kernel vocabulary -- no non-probabilistic definition of Belief exists anywhere in the corpus.

rows.anchor: No probability space (Omega,F,P) is constructed anywhere. The triple is mentioned once (v1 §30) as a conditional ('becomes useful when…').
rows.statement: No formal probability space is ever constructed anywhere in the statistical layer; the (Omega,F,P) triple is mentioned exactly once, only as a hypothetical conditional.

rows.anchor: Model averaging P(D)=sum_m P(D|M_m)P(M_m) (082 §82.36) — prior over models P(M_m) used, never justified.
rows.statement: A model-averaging formula uses a prior over models P(M_m) that is never justified or constructed anywhere in the source.

rows.anchor: Load-bearing gap: every P(E|H) assumes a likelihood is obtainable for organizational/architectural evidence; no file says where it would come from.
rows.statement: Identifies a load-bearing gap: every likelihood P(E|H) used throughout the statistical layer assumes such a likelihood is obtainable for organizational/architectural evidence, but no file ever explains where such a likelihood would actually come from.

rows.anchor: Master rule (v1): S_{t+1} = U_R(S_t, E|C) — regime-indexed update. U_R has no axioms, no type signature beyond this, no existence/uniqueness conditions; characterized only by instances
rows.statement: The corpus's proposed master evidence-update rule S_{t+1}=U_R(S_t,E|C) has no axioms, no type signature beyond its bare shape, and no existence or uniqueness conditions -- it is characterized only by a list of example instances (Bayesian, Dempster-Shafer, fuzzy, non-monotonic, argumentation, epistemic logic, KST).

rows.anchor: Epistemic Representation Invariance (v1 §28–29): task-equivalence of regimes via semantics-preserving phi — self-declared 'candidate mathematical definition, not a theorem we have proved'.
rows.statement: Records the Epistemic Representation Invariance concept (task-equivalence of different evidence-combination regimes via a semantics-preserving mapping) as self-declared by its own source to be a candidate mathematical definition, explicitly not a proven theorem.

rows.anchor: v2 kernel-substrate claim: S_min = intersection_R Requirements(R) = (D, E_{<=t}, Source, Time, Uncertainty) — self-declared research hypothesis; the intersection is asserted, not derived, over incommensurable requirement sets, and none of the five members appears literally in any per-regime tuple.
rows.statement: A proposed minimal kernel substrate (intersection of per-regime requirements, yielding five named members) is a self-declared research hypothesis whose intersection is merely asserted, not actually derived, over sets the register notes are incommensurable -- and none of the five claimed member requirements literally appears in any actual per-regime tuple.

rows.anchor: KST's local independence r(R,K) (beta_q careless error, eta_q lucky guess) is adopted into the reconstruction schema while its own ASSUMPTION list is not carried over with it.
rows.statement: The Knowledge Space Theory local-independence machinery is adopted into the KnowledgeOS reconstruction schema without carrying over its own source assumption list -- an unflagged import of an external technique stripped of its preconditions.

rows.anchor: Governing law: uncertainty must never disappear merely because the representation changed (§82.71 clarifies: not monotone increase — semantic preservation). Seven new invariants (§82.72): I_UncertaintyPreservation · I_Dependence · I_ModelUncertainty · I_Calibration · I_EpistemicPrecision · I_Decisio
rows.statement: Records the uncertainty-propagation chapter's governing law (uncertainty must never silently vanish through representation change, meaning semantic preservation, not required monotone increase) and its own set of seven named invariants.

rows.anchor: All 33 'falsification experiments' are detection expectations; nothing was executed; PASS = author's expectation matches author's prescription.
rows.statement: A sharp verifier observation: all 33 named 'falsification experiments' in the uncertainty-propagation chapter are merely detection expectations that were never actually executed -- their recorded 'PASS' verdicts only mean the author's stated expectation matched the author's own prescription, not that anything was empirically tested.

rows.anchor: SNF file's own critique half demotes the review half: d is structural, not semantic distance; entropy is model-relative; composite Q_snf REJECTED (unjustified weights; worked FAIL case); ... header 'MATHEMATICALLY UNDERSPECIFIED' (K6).
rows.statement: K6 (SNF measurement framework): the file's own internal critique half demotes its review half's claims point by point (distance metric is structural not semantic, entropy is model-relative, a composite score is rejected with a worked failure case, thresholds are demoted to merely experimental) -- the review half's claim that 'all metrics have known statistical properties' is directly contradicted by the file's own header labeling itself 'MATHEMATICALLY UNDERSPECIFIED'.

rows.anchor: Experiments: v0.1 synthetic pilot only (non-collapse 0/20 at threshold; CR 25% — on deliberately collapsed synthetic data); v0.2/v0.3 produced no exposed numbers, and the file explicitly refuses to invent them.
rows.statement: The SNF framework's only actual empirical results come from a v0.1 synthetic pilot (0/20 non-collapse at threshold, 25% collision rate on deliberately collapsed synthetic data); the file itself explicitly refuses to invent numbers for the later, unexecuted v0.2/v0.3 versions.

rows.anchor: Strongest positive claim: KST reconstruction O_{<=t} -> P(K_t|O_{<=t}) -> K-hat_t with convergence 'under conditions' ... The KnowledgeOS analogue of the structure K has never been constructed; the schema transferred without its precondition.
rows.statement: The corpus's single strongest positive statistical claim (a Knowledge Space Theory reconstruction result with a cited convergence theorem) is transferred into KnowledgeOS without ever constructing the actual knowledge-structure object the theorem's convergence conditions require -- the schema is imported without its own precondition.

rows.anchor: Strongest negative discipline (Freedman): NOT_IDENTIFIABLE as first-class successful outcome; causal identification gate (IDENTIFIED / PARTIALLY / NOT / UNKNOWN); diagnostics cannot validate model assumptions from data alone.
rows.statement: Records the corpus's strongest adopted negative statistical discipline (from Freedman): treating NOT_IDENTIFIABLE as a legitimate first-class successful outcome (not a failure), a four-valued causal identification gate, and the principle that diagnostics alone can never validate a model's own assumptions from data.

rows.anchor: Richest vocabulary (027 §27.41): Missing / Unknown / NotApplicable / NotObserved / Withheld / Contradictory — none of the six individually defined; MCAR/MAR/MNAR named, not defined.
rows.statement: The richest missingness vocabulary in the corpus (six distinct null-like categories) has none of its six members individually defined, and the standard missing-data mechanisms MCAR/MAR/MNAR are named but never actually defined.

rows.anchor: The proposed kernel tuple S_Kernel=(D,E,S,T,U) has no slot for absence — non-observation/withheld/inapplicable have nowhere to live. ... KST adoption internalizes q not-in K = 'not mastered' — exactly the unknown-vs-zero conflation 027 forbids; unflagged in the file.
rows.statement: The proposed five-element kernel tuple has no slot at all for absence/missingness, so non-observation, withheld, and inapplicable data have nowhere to be represented; separately, the adopted Knowledge Space Theory machinery internalizes 'not in the knowledge state' as meaning 'not mastered' -- exactly the Unknown-vs-Zero conflation the same corpus elsewhere explicitly forbids, and this conflation is unflagged where it is imported.

rows.anchor: Master (Freedman): 'No inference without an explicit inferential basis' — Data -> Observation -> Interpretation -> Inference -> Claim, never Data -> AI says X -> Knowledge = X. ... Ten invariants verbatim ... Internal tension: the same file's Inference schema carries a bare confidence: field its own
rows.statement: Records the Freedman-derived master discipline (no inference without an explicit inferential basis, forbidding a direct Data->AI-says-X->Knowledge=X shortcut) and its ten adopted invariants, but flags (K16) that the very same file's own Inference schema still carries a bare scalar confidence field that its own earlier sections argue against.

rows.anchor: HA-S05 Model prior P(M_m): exhaustive+exclusive model set and prior existence unstated (082 §82.36). ... HA-S08 Cardinal, cross-state-comparable utility assumed by EU (027 §27.55) — unexamined against the corpus's own measurement-theory standard.
rows.statement: Two of the twelve highest-risk hidden assumptions: model averaging silently assumes an exhaustive and mutually exclusive model set with an existing prior (never stated), and the expected-utility decision formula silently assumes cardinal, cross-state-comparable utility, never examined against the corpus's own adopted (Roberts) measurement-theory standard.

rows.anchor: HA-S10 U_R assumed total/deterministic and phi_R assumed to exist for each regime — the entire regime architecture proceeds on an unproved existence claim. ... HA-S12 All PASS verdicts presuppose an executed system; none exists.
rows.statement: Two more highest-risk hidden assumptions: the entire multi-regime evidence-combination architecture proceeds on an unproved existence claim (that the update function U_R is total/deterministic and a semantics-preserving mapping phi_R exists for every regime), and every recorded 'PASS' verdict anywhere in this statistical layer presupposes an executed system that in fact does not exist.

rows.anchor: K10 Eight distinct 'the epistemic object is a tuple' definitions (arity 5–13) with no mapping between any two.
rows.statement: K10: eight mutually distinct tuple definitions for 'the epistemic object' exist across the corpus, ranging in arity from 5 to 13 elements, with no mapping ever given between any two of them.

rows.anchor: K9 Unknown operationalized 4+ incompatible ways (status enum · E5 member · absent from decision vocabulary · entropy threshold · split into INCONCLUSIVE/INSUFFICIENT). ... K11 Systematic notation collisions ... including U as utility and uncertainty within step-027.
rows.statement: K9: 'Unknown' is operationalized in at least four incompatible ways across the corpus (a status enum value, an epistemic-status-set member, absent from the decision vocabulary entirely, an entropy threshold, and split into two further sub-values). K11: systematic notation collisions exist throughout, including the symbol U meaning both utility and uncertainty within the very same source file.

rows.anchor: K12 'Conservation of uncertainty' vs explicit denial of monotonicity — conservation language for a non-erasure requirement; no conserved quantity stated.
rows.statement: K12: the corpus's own 'conservation of uncertainty' language (echoed at this batch's Step 199/S1417 as invariant I_67) is in tension with its explicit denial that uncertainty must monotonically increase -- 'conservation' is used loosely for a non-erasure requirement without any actual conserved quantity ever being stated.

rows.anchor: Consolidated undefined terms (statistical layer): U(H) component domains · q in Q(E,q) · VOI (two informal, different forms) · P membership · U (both the uncertainty set and the kernel slot) · interaction terms · MCAR/MAR/MNAR · the six null semantics individually · full E5 semantics · Combine · the
rows.statement: Consolidates a long list of symbols/terms used throughout the statistical layer that are never actually defined (uncertainty-vector component domains, evidence-quality parameter q, two different informal notions of Value of Information, imprecise-probability set membership, the overloaded symbol U, interaction terms, missingness mechanisms, the six null semantics, full epistemic-status semantics, a Combine operator, KST update parameters, the SNF consistency estimand, a requirements universe, and equivalence relation symbols).

rows.anchor: each Q-file is a three-layer document — original definition → reviewer critique rejecting parts of it → (Q15/Q20 only) a revised definition. Q13 and Q14 have no revised section ... downstream files (Q20 §3.1) cite the unrevised Q13 10-tuple as authoritative.
rows.statement: Structural finding across the Q-series files: each is a three-layer document (original definition, reviewer critique, sometimes a revision); two of the four (Q13, Q14) were never revised despite their own critiques standing unresolved, and a later file cites the unrevised, already-critiqued Q13 form as authoritative regardless.

rows.anchor: Grep-verified absence: the token 'axiom'/'postulate' occurs zero times in all eleven files. The corpus's axiom-role objects are numbered invariants and 'freeze' lists.
rows.statement: Confirms via direct grep across all eleven read files that the words 'axiom' and 'postulate' never appear even once; the corpus's functional axiom-role objects are instead its numbered invariants and ad hoc 'freeze' lists.

rows.anchor: Direct incompatibility of the two 'revised' models: Q15-revised puts Zero/Lord findings inside both K_t and S_t; Q20-revised excludes them from S_t by invariant. Step 203 rejects the very product construction Q20-revised adopts. Neither cites the other.
rows.statement: Identifies a direct three-way incompatibility: Q15's own revised model places Zero/Lord findings inside both K_t and S_t; Q20's own revised model excludes them from S_t by an explicit invariant; and this batch's Step 203 (S1422) rejects the product-state construction that Q20-revised actually adopts -- none of the three formulations cites or acknowledges either of the others.

rows.anchor: T7 K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t) ... T8 K_t=Replay(K_0,H_t). Typed: delta: K x E -/-> K (explicitly partial); ... defects recorded in-place: transition rules emit 6-tuples containing Z_t,L_t against the same section's T5; Rollback rule written as plain equality while its own prose demands different provena
rows.statement: The Q15-revised transition model, described as the most-developed 'frozen' candidate with eight numbered theorems, contains internal defects recorded in place: its own transition rules emit tuples containing Zero/Lord findings that violate its own Theorem T5 (Zero evaluates but does not constitute Knowledge), its rollback rule is written as a plain equality that contradicts its own prose's provenance requirements, two symbols are used but never defined, and a precondition's argument order is reversed between two sections of the same document.

rows.anchor: 13 types {E,D,V,P,A,R,E_v,Sigma,H,Z,L,K,I} ... claimed 'epistemic lattice' Sigma1<=Sigma2 — rejected by its own review (Resolution not naturally ordered; product order != lattice). Evidence-support scalar Supports in [-1,1] rejected by review in favor of (Bearing,Strength).
rows.statement: Records that Q14's own thirteen-type universe includes a claimed 'epistemic lattice' structure that its own internal review rejects (the proposed order is not naturally a lattice), and a scalar evidence-support measure that the same review replaces with a two-component (Bearing, Strength) pair instead.

rows.anchor: Impossibility (step-031 §31.19, verbatim): if Omega(W1)=Omega(W2) while W1!=W2, KnowledgeOS cannot distinguish them from observations alone — 'No algorithm can recover information that the observation function destroys.'
rows.statement: Records the corpus's strongest candidate formal impossibility result: if two distinct world states produce the same observation-function output, no algorithm can recover the lost distinguishing information from observations alone -- correctly stated but noted as a standard information-theoretic fact the corpus calls 'one of the strongest mathematical foundations'.

rows.anchor: step-031's 20 numbered counterexamples (§31.49–68), all PASS conceptually — conceptual, not executed; §31.69 grades J (uncertainty propagation), K (proof calculus), L (complexity) OPEN.
rows.statement: Notes that step-031's twenty numbered counterexamples all 'pass' only conceptually (never actually executed), and the same document leaves three whole areas (uncertainty propagation, proof calculus, computational complexity) explicitly graded OPEN.

rows.anchor: Freeze lists (assumption-by-fiat): Step 201 §201.40 (16+2) · Q14 review §18 ('freeze now' 9 / 'do NOT freeze' 5 ...) · Q20 review §25 (11 boxed invariants incl. S_t=Replay(S_0,H_t) conditional on determinism + policy/version refs) · Step 203 Event!=State.
rows.statement: Inventories the corpus's several independent 'freeze list' (assumption-by-fiat) mechanisms across different files, including this batch's own Step 201 sixteen-plus-two freeze (S1420) and Step 203's Event!=State freeze (S1422), alongside two unrelated Q-series freeze lists that were never reconciled with the Step 201/203 ones.

rows.anchor: Self-limitations: step-031 §31.75 'Formal completeness: NOT YET' ... Q20 review denies 'complete mathematical specification' — which the Q20 revised half then reinstates (I.12); Gita = conceptual lens only, stated in 189/201/202/204.
rows.statement: Notes step-031's own honest 'formal completeness: NOT YET' self-limitation, contrasted with Q20 where a completeness claim is made, then denied by its own review, then silently reinstated by its own later revision (I.12) -- and confirms the Gita-as-conceptual-lens-only discipline is consistently stated across this batch's own Steps 189/201/202/204 (S1390, S1420, S1421, S1423).

rows.statement: I.1 and I.9 from the 29-item contradiction inventory: seven incompatible K_t tuple forms persist with none ever retracted, and systematic single-glyph notation collisions run throughout the corpus (e.g. the same symbol variously meaning entity, evidence, or events; or context, conflicts, commands, or constraints; or a transition contract in one place and an unrelated four-vector elsewhere in the same file).
