aliases: Linga as Kernel, Yoni as Transformation Field

sources.note: Sharper, falsifiable successor to the Yoni Lens formulation: Kernel produces a differentiated projection P_t, Yoni transforms it into an offspring/K_{t+1}; includes attack tests (Linga-necessity, Yoni-necessity, same-projection-different-field, same-field-different-projection, four-combination matrix) and three null hypotheses (H0-A/B/C).

rows.anchor: K_t --𝒦--> P_t --𝒴--> K_{t+1} ... 𝒦(K_t,Q_t) → P_t produces an epistemic projection/contribution. ... The critical hypothesis is: 𝒦 = initiating differentiation, not merely 'storage.'
rows.statement: Sharpens the Linga/Yoni model into K_t -[Kernel]-> P_t -[Yoni]-> K_{t+1}, with Kernel(K_t,Q_t)->P_t producing a differentiated epistemic projection (proposal/hypothesis/assertion/question/candidate interpretation/expected state/candidate action); central hypothesis: the kernel is initiating differentiation, not merely storage.

rows.anchor: 𝒴(P_t, E_t, H_t, C_t, S_t, R_t) → O_t where O_t is the candidate offspring. ... Offspring ≠ Knowledge. Instead: Offspring = K_{t+1} as our candidate hypothesis.
rows.statement: Defines the Yoni transformation Yoni(P_t,E_t,H_t,C_t,S_t,R_t)->O_t (candidate offspring), producing revised/unresolved/rejected/determined/new-hypothesis/conflict/closure outcomes; candidate hypothesis Offspring=K_{t+1}, explicitly Offspring != Knowledge.

rows.anchor: the kernel is the irreducible capacity to produce a differentiated epistemic contribution into the field. ... 𝒦: (K_t,Q_t) ↦ P_t. Then the Yoni transformation: 𝒴: (P_t,E_t,H_t,C_t,S_t,R_t) ↦ K_{t+1}.
rows.statement: Proposes reinterpreting the kernel not as 'a set of operators that processes knowledge' but as 'the irreducible capacity to produce a differentiated epistemic contribution into the field' -- a Linga-like reading, formalized as Kernel:(K_t,Q_t)->P_t feeding Yoni:(P_t,E_t,H_t,C_t,S_t,R_t)->K_{t+1}.

rows.anchor: Is the Linga actually necessary? Suppose K_t → Yoni → K_{t+1} can produce exactly the same behavior. Then: Linga is not an independent capability ... Construct a case where the Yoni cannot generate a meaningful transformation without a differentiated input. Then we obtain evidence for: Reception requires a distinguishable projection.
rows.statement: First attack test: check whether Yoni alone (without a distinct Linga/Kernel projection step) reproduces all behavior -- if so, Linga is not an independent capability; if constructing a case shows Yoni cannot transform meaningfully without a differentiated input, that is evidence 'reception requires a distinguishable projection.'

rows.anchor: Second attack: is Yoni actually necessary? Construct: K_t --𝒦--> P_t --𝒦--> K_{t+1} with no separate transformation field. If this reproduces all behavior, then: Yoni adds no independent capability. But if typed evidence, challenge, alternatives, contextual relations, etc. require a distinct relational transformation environment, then we have evidence for: Projection ≠ Transformation.
rows.statement: Second attack test: check whether applying the Kernel operator twice (K_t->P_t->K_{t+1}, no separate Yoni field) reproduces all behavior -- if so, Yoni adds no independent capability; if typed evidence/challenge/alternatives/contextual relations require a distinct relational transformation environment, that is evidence Projection != Transformation.

rows.anchor: Case A: P_1=H, E_1⊨H → K_{t+1}: H determined. Case B: P_1=H, E_1⊨¬H → K_{t+1}: H rejected. Case C: P_1=H, E_1=∅ → K_{t+1}: H unresolved. The Linga is identical. The Yoni field determines the transformation. ... Same Projection + Different Field ⇒ Different Offspring.
rows.statement: Designs the 'same projection, different field' test: holding the Kernel's projection P_1=H fixed while varying the evidence field (entailing H, entailing not-H, or empty) yields three different offspring (determined/rejected/unresolved) -- if this holds under formal testing, it shows Same Projection + Different Field => Different Offspring, i.e. the Yoni concept does real explanatory work.

rows.anchor: Hold 𝒴_t constant. Then vary P_1, P_2, P_3 ... This tests whether the two poles are functionally distinguishable.
rows.statement: Designs the reverse 'same field, different projection' test: holding Y_t constant while varying the Kernel's projection (P_1,P_2,P_3, e.g. H, not-H, H2) and observing distinct outputs K_1,K_2,K_3, testing whether the Linga and Yoni poles are functionally distinguishable.

rows.anchor: | Projection | Field | Expected question | absent/absent: Can anything emerge? | present/absent: Can projection alone generate offspring? | absent/present: Can field generate offspring without projection? | present/present: Does interaction generate a distinct offspring? Projection + Field → Transformation while neither alone is sufficient. But we must let the experiment falsify that.
rows.statement: Specifies a four-combination adversarial presence/absence matrix over {Projection, Field} to test whether Projection+Field->Transformation while neither factor alone is sufficient, explicitly requiring the experiment (not intuition) to decide this.

rows.anchor: The offspring should initially be typed as: O_{t+1} ∈ {K_{t+1}, Revision, Hypothesis, Rejection, Conflict, Uncertainty, ClosureEvent, ...} ... I suspect the strongest formulation will be: Offspring = Emergent Epistemic Product rather than: Offspring = Knowledge. That lets a failed inquiry still produce an epistemically meaningful result.
rows.statement: Types the offspring as a sum type O_{t+1} in {K_{t+1}, Revision, Hypothesis, Rejection, Conflict, Uncertainty, ClosureEvent, ...}, favoring 'Offspring = Emergent Epistemic Product' over 'Offspring = Knowledge' so a failed inquiry ('the available evidence cannot determine H') still counts as a legitimate epistemic outcome.

rows.anchor: KR-LINGA-YONI-2026-09-02 ... central hypothesis: 𝒦_Linga → 𝒴_Transform → O_Offspring ... H0-A Linga and Yoni are not functionally distinguishable. H0-B Yoni is merely a different description of ordinary state transition. H0-C Offspring is merely another name for K_{t+1}, with no additional useful semantics.
rows.statement: Names the decisive experiment KR-LINGA-YONI-2026-09-02 with central hypothesis Kernel_Linga->Yoni_Transform->Offspring and three explicit null hypotheses to falsify: H0-A (Linga/Yoni not functionally distinguishable), H0-B (Yoni merely redescribes ordinary state transition), H0-C (Offspring merely another name for K_{t+1} with no added semantics).

rows.anchor: If the experiment succeeds, we should not immediately conclude that the kernel is Linga. Instead, the result could be: Kernel has a Linga-like functional pole. ... Is the kernel the whole epistemic process, or is it the minimal initiating mechanism embedded in a larger epistemic field?
rows.statement: Even a successful experiment would not license concluding 'the kernel is Linga' -- only the safer 'the kernel has a Linga-like functional pole', reopening the standing kernel-scope question: is the kernel the whole epistemic process or the minimal initiating mechanism embedded in a larger epistemic field, testable without assuming the answer.

rows.anchor: I do not yet agree with the document's stronger identity claims such as: 𝒦 ≡ Linga or KnowledgeOS = Linga(Kernel) × Yoni(Field). Those should be the hypothesis we test, not the conclusion.
rows.statement: Rejects the source document's identity claims Kernel-equiv-Linga and 'KnowledgeOS=Linga(Kernel)xYoni(Field)' as premature conclusions, insisting they be treated as hypotheses to test.

rows.anchor: K_t --𝒦?--> P_t --𝒴--> O_t ... and then test whether: O_t ≅ K_{t+1}. That is a much cleaner research model [than 'Kernel → Assertion → Knowledge State'].
rows.statement: Replaces the source document's 'Kernel -> Assertion -> Knowledge State' formulation with K_t -[candidate active Kernel K?]-> P_t -[Yoni transformation]-> O_t, then tests whether O_t is isomorphic to K_{t+1}.

rows.anchor: 'The Linga-Kernel is the proposer' and 'the Linga-Kernel transforms the Yoni.' This suggests two different functions: Linga initiates/differentiates/projects. Yoni receives/relates/transforms. Therefore: Initiation ≠ Transformation.
rows.statement: Identifies the deepest recoverable insight in the source document: two different functions, Linga (initiates/differentiates/projects) and Yoni (receives/relates/transforms), giving Initiation != Transformation -- if the kernel is only the irreducible initiating mechanism, this could explain why the kernel is small while the epistemic field is much richer.

rows.anchor: Zero is no longer part of Yoni's identity. It becomes the mechanism/lens that examines the offspring after emergence. Likewise, Lord and Sārathi do not need to become 'parts of the Linga.' ... I would instead keep them as independent candidate lenses/responsibilities until we test otherwise.
rows.statement: Explicitly separates Zero (an independent lens examining the offspring after emergence, not part of Yoni's identity) and Lord/Sarathi (independent candidate lenses/responsibilities, not sub-parts of Linga) from the Linga/Yoni model -- correcting the source document's mapping of Lord/Sarathi as Linga components.

rows.anchor: Model A - Conventional: K_t --Θ--> K_{t+1}. Model B - Yoni-centered: K_t → Yoni → K_{t+1}. Model C - Linga-Yoni: K_t → Linga → Yoni → Offspring → K_{t+1}. ... Does Model C distinguish epistemic phenomena that Models A and B cannot distinguish? ... If no, then Linga-Yoni is a powerful philosophical interpretation but formally redundant.
rows.statement: Proposes a decisive three-model comparative test: Model A (conventional K_t-Theta->K_{t+1}), Model B (Yoni-centered, K_t->Yoni->K_{t+1}), Model C (Linga-Yoni, K_t->Linga->Yoni->Offspring->K_{t+1}); the real experiment asks whether Model C distinguishes epistemic phenomena the simpler Models A and B cannot -- if not, Linga-Yoni is formally redundant despite philosophical appeal.

rows.anchor: | Yoni can represent a receptive/transformative field | [PROP] Strong | | Linga can represent an active epistemic principle | [PROP] Strong | | Linga is the Kernel | [OPEN] | ... | Offspring = Knowledge | [NEG] Too strong | | Offspring = Truth | [NEG] Reject | | Offspring = new epistemic product/state | [PROP] Strong candidate | | Reconciliation = orgasm/offspring | [NEG] Not supported | | Closure = temporal event | [EXP] Supported by prior experiment |
rows.statement: Comprehensive claim-by-claim verdict table across thirteen claims in the Linga/Yoni track, ranging from [PROP] Strong (Yoni as field, Linga as active principle) through [OPEN] (Linga is the Kernel; Linga/Yoni as architecture components) to [NEG] (Offspring=Knowledge too strong, Offspring=Truth reject, Reconciliation=orgasm/offspring not supported) to [EXP] (Closure as temporal event, supported by the prior closure experiment) -- concluding that Linga/Yoni as a theoretical lens is currently the strongest defensible position.

rows.anchor: Kernel may exhibit a Linga-like active principle, while Yoni represents the transformative epistemic field. Then we test whether the Linga-Yoni-Offspring triad is actually structurally necessary. ... rigorous enough that the experiment can genuinely prove the metaphor wrong if the existing KnowledgeOS theory already explains everything without it.
rows.statement: Converts the source document's declaration 'Kernel=Linga' into the research hypothesis 'Kernel may exhibit a Linga-like active principle, while Yoni represents the transformative epistemic field', to be tested for whether the Linga-Yoni-Offspring triad is structurally necessary, with the experiment explicitly capable of proving the metaphor wrong if existing theory already explains everything without it.

rows.anchor: Linga is NOT the Kernel. Yoni is NOT the Kernel. The Linga-Yoni triad is a HYPOTHESIS about epistemic generation, not a claim about existing architecture. ... Hypothesis → Test → Falsify → Revise.
rows.statement: Formal ruling: the Linga-Yoni triad is accepted only as a research hypothesis, explicitly not a claim that Linga or Yoni is the Kernel or existing architecture, governed by the cycle Hypothesis->Test->Falsify->Revise.

rows.anchor: | Function | Linga | Yoni | Initiation ✅ ❌ | Differentiation ✅ ❌ | Proposal ✅ ❌ | Projection ✅ ❌ | Reception ❌ ✅ | Relation ❌ ✅ | Challenge ❌ ✅ | Assessment ❌ ✅ | Reconciliation ❌ ✅ | Transformation ❌ ✅
rows.statement: Formalizes a strict functional separation table: Linga owns Initiation/Differentiation/Proposal/Projection exclusively; Yoni owns Reception/Relation/Challenge/Assessment/Reconciliation/Transformation exclusively, with no overlap.

rows.anchor: Kernel = Linga | Too strong; Linga is one function among many | Offspring = Knowledge | Offspring may contain uncertainty, conflict, hypotheses | Offspring = Truth | The active principle cannot 'bring truth into existence' | Reconciliation = Orgasm | Reconciliation is a process, not an event | Closure = Temporal Event | Closure is a condition, not necessarily an event | Lord Lens = Linga's Vision | Lord is an independent lens; mapping is metaphorical
rows.statement: Formal reject-list with stated reasons: Kernel=Linga (too strong, Linga is one function among many), Offspring=Knowledge (offspring may contain uncertainty/conflict/hypotheses), Offspring=Truth (the active principle cannot bring truth into existence), Reconciliation=Orgasm (reconciliation is a process not an event), Closure=Temporal-Event (closure is a condition not necessarily an event -- noted as in tension with the KR-CLOSURE experiment's own event-vs-state finding), Lord-Lens=Linga's-Vision (Lord is an independent lens, the mapping is only metaphorical).

rows.anchor: K_{t+1} = Offspring(Yoni(Linga(K_t, Q_t), E_t, H_t, C_t, S_t, R_t)).
rows.statement: States the complete composed equation for the accepted research hypothesis: K_{t+1}=Offspring(Yoni(Linga(K_t,Q_t),E_t,H_t,C_t,S_t,R_t)).

rows.anchor: LY-H1 Initiation is distinguishable from transformation ... LY-H2 Transformation requires a receptive field ... LY-H3 Emergent products are not reducible to inputs ... LY-H4 Zero examines offspring, not the field ... LY-H5 The cycle is necessary.
rows.statement: States five formal hypotheses (LY-H1..H5, distinct numbering from the earlier YL-H1..H6): initiation-distinguishable-from-transformation, transformation-requires-a-receptive-field, emergent-products-not-reducible-to-inputs, Zero-examines-offspring-not-the-field, and cycle-necessity, each paired with a named test (Linga vs Yoni functions; Yoni necessity test; Offspring!=Input; Zero-Yoni separation; removal test).

rows.anchor: Test LY-T1 -- Initiation vs Transformation: Setup: K0, Q0. Execute: P0=Linga(K0,Q0); O0=Yoni(P0,E0,H0,C0,S0,R0); K1=Offspring(O0). Measure: Is P0 distinguishable from O0? Pass if: P0≠O0, Initiation function≠Transformation function. Fail if: P0=O0.
rows.statement: Specifies the concrete LY-T1 empirical protocol (the only one given in full): construct P0=Linga(K0,Q0), then O0=Yoni(P0,E0,H0,C0,S0,R0), then K1=Offspring(O0); pass condition is P0!=O0 with initiation and transformation functions genuinely distinct; fail condition is P0=O0.

experiment.assumptions: Linga and Yoni are implementable as distinct functions
experiment.method: compute P0=Linga(K0,Q0), then O0=Yoni(P0,E0,H0,C0,S0,R0), then K1=Offspring(O0); check P0 vs O0

rows.anchor: STEP 282 -- LINGA-YONI TRIAID EMPIRICAL TEST. Objective: Determine whether the Linga-Yoni triad reveals structural properties not visible in the conventional KnowledgeOS model. ... Success Criterion: Model C distinguishes cases that Models A and B cannot. Failure Criterion: Model C offers no additional distinguishability.
rows.statement: Commissions STEP 282 (Linga-Yoni Triad Empirical Test) as the concrete next research step: implement Models A/B/C, generate adversarial cases, compare distinguishability, with success defined as Model C distinguishing cases Models A/B cannot and failure as no additional distinguishability -- no corresponding result file for STEP 282 appears in this batch.

rows.anchor: it works much better as a model of the Gita's epistemic dynamics than as a claim that the Gita itself teaches a 'Linga-Yoni epistemology.' ... Linga-Yoni may provide a complementary polarity for modelling how epistemic activity enters and transforms a field.
rows.statement: Corrects the framing of Linga-Yoni relative to the Gita: it should be introduced only as a secondary interpretive lens over the Gita's own extracted structures (Ksetra, Ksetrajna, discrimination, action/consequence, inquiry/discipline), not as a claim that the Gita itself teaches a Linga-Yoni epistemology.

rows.anchor: Linga ≈ active/initiating principle and: Yoni ≈ receptive/manifesting field. Their interaction produces a changing manifestation: Linga + Yoni → Manifestation → Experience → Knowledge/realization. ... The Gita does not establish this equation. It is our philosophical model layered onto the text.
rows.statement: Proposes Linga~active/initiating principle and Yoni~receptive/manifesting field, whose interaction yields Manifestation->Experience->Knowledge/realization, explicitly flagged as a philosophical model layered onto the Gita text, not something the Gita itself establishes; traces the provenance chain Gita source -> interpretation -> Linga-Yoni analogy -> KnowledgeOS hypothesis.

rows.anchor: We can derive mathematics inspired by the Linga-Yoni structure, but we cannot derive mathematical theorems from the Gita or from the metaphor itself. The productive route is to treat the Gita/Linga-Yoni correspondence as a structural hypothesis, then ask what mathematical structure naturally represents that hypothesis.
rows.statement: States a sharp methodological distinction: mathematics can be inspired by the Linga-Yoni structure, but no mathematical theorem can be derived FROM the Gita or the metaphor itself -- the correspondence is treated as a structural hypothesis whose natural mathematical representation is then sought.

rows.anchor: L: (K_t,Q_t)→P_t ... Y:(P_t,K_t,E_t,C_t,S_t)→K_{t+1}. ... the two operators have different domains/codomains and therefore are not interchangeable. That gives us: L≠Y unless there exists a structure-preserving isomorphism ... This mathematically reflects: Generation ≠ Transformation.
rows.statement: First derivation: L:(K_t,Q_t)->P_t and Y:(P_t,K_t,E_t,C_t,S_t)->K_{t+1} have provably different domains/codomains, hence L!=Y absent a structure-preserving isomorphism (none currently evidenced) -- mathematically grounding Generation != Transformation.

rows.anchor: O_t = μ(L_t,Y_t,E_t,…). Then: K_{t+1}=Θ(K_t,O_t). ... But crucially: O_t ≠ K_{t+1} necessarily. And: O_t ≠ Truth. And: O_t ≠ Knowledge necessarily. The offspring can be: a new hypothesis, a revised representation, a contradiction, a rejected proposition, a determination, an unresolved question, or genuinely attributed knowledge.
rows.statement: Formalizes offspring as O_t=mu(L_t,Y_t,E_t,...) feeding K_{t+1}=Theta(K_t,O_t), with O_t not necessarily equal to K_{t+1}, Truth, or Knowledge -- the offspring may be any of: new hypothesis, revised representation, contradiction, rejected proposition, determination, unresolved question, or genuinely attributed knowledge.

rows.anchor: 1. Action: Can Linga-Yoni be represented naturally as an action α:𝓛×𝓨→𝓨? 2. Composition ... 3. Invariants ... 4. Progress: Can an epistemic partial order ≽ be defined without circularity? 5. Minimality: Is the Linga/Yoni factorization mathematically necessary, or can K_t→K_{t+1} represent exactly the same observable behavior? The fifth question is the decisive one.
rows.statement: States a five-question mathematical research programme (Action, Composition, Invariants, Progress, Minimality) for the Linga-Yoni factorization, identifying the fifth (minimality: is Theta=YoL mathematically necessary or reducible to an ordinary transition operator) as decisive -- if reducible, Linga-Yoni is a beautiful metaphor adding no mathematical structure; if the factorization reveals invariants/non-commutativity/observability properties not representable without the two stages, it is mathematically substantive.

rows.anchor: Yoni becomes a metaphor for: the structured space in which candidate states interact and transform. Mathematical abstraction: (𝓗,𝓡,Θ) ... Linga becomes a metaphor for: G: K_t × Q_t → 𝓗_t -- candidate generation. ... Linga-like → Generation → Candidate Space → Assessment → Selection → Transformation.
rows.statement: Places the final Linga/Yoni interpretation inside the structure-first framework: Yoni as (H,R,Theta) -- the structured candidate space with relations and transformations -- and Linga as G:K_t x Q_t -> H_t (candidate generation), both explicitly [EXT] external lenses, not domain objects, feeding a Generation->CandidateSpace->Assessment->Selection->Transformation pipeline.

Construct a case where the Yoni cannot generate a meaningful transformation without a differentiated input. Then we obtain evidence for: Reception requires a distinguishable projection.

rationale_evidence.statement: Comprehensive claim-by-claim verdict table across thirteen claims in the Linga/Yoni track, ranging from [PROP] Strong (Yoni as field, Linga as active principle) through [OPEN] (Linga is the Kernel; Linga/Yoni as architecture components) to [NEG] (Offspring=Knowledge too strong, Offspring=Truth reject, Reconciliation=orgasm/offspring not supported) to [EXP] (Closure as temporal event, supported by the prior closure experiment) -- concluding that Linga/Yoni as a theoretical lens is currently the strongest defensible position.

That gives us: L≠Y unless there exists a structure-preserving isomorphism ... This mathematically reflects: Generation ≠ Transformation.

sources.note: S0892's Step 25C: derives idempotency, independence-vs-identity, dependency, conflict!=uncertainty, temporal fit, reliability!=relevance, and authenticity!=correctness from eight experiments; derives commutativity/associativity with a temporal-context qualification; establishes the three-layer Evidence!=Assessment!=Inference separation; evaluates and refuses to select among Bayesian/Dempster-Shafer/fuzzy/weighted-scoring (all Candidate, not selected); proposes four DDD bounded contexts and seven falsification tests; verdicts CONDITIONAL PASS with C1-C6 open items; hands off to Step 25C.1 (compare candidate evidence algebras).

rows.anchor: Given multiple pieces of evidence, how can KnowledgeOS combine them into an assessment without double-counting, losing uncertainty, or manufacturing certainty? I will deliberately not choose Bayesian probability, Dempster–Shafer, fuzzy logic, weighted scoring, or another framework yet. First we deri
rows.statement: States the governing method for Step 25C: derive required algebraic properties for evidence aggregation before selecting any specific mathematical framework.

rows.anchor: 25C.1 — Start with the simplest case ... Assess(H,E_1)=0.8. Why? Because the number 0.8 has no defined semantics. Does it mean 80% probability that H is true? 80% confidence? 80% source reliability? 80% evidence strength? 80% decision readiness? These are different things. No numerical value without
rows.statement: Reaffirms the rule 'no numerical value without defined semantics' — a bare 0.8 could mean five different incompatible things.

rows.anchor: 25C.2 — Separate the dimensions ... Assessment(H,E) = (R,D,T,A,I,C,U) where relevance; directness; temporal fit; authenticity; independence; consistency; uncertainty. This is not yet the final structure. It is an experimental decomposition. ... 25C.3 — Evidence support relation ... Supports(E,H) and
rows.statement: Defines a seven-dimension Assessment tuple (Relevance,Directness,TemporalFit,Authenticity,Independence,Consistency,Uncertainty) and a four-valued qualitative Support relation {Support,Challenge,Neutral,Unknown}.

rows.anchor: 25C.4 — Experiment A: duplicate evidence ... byte-for-byte identical copies. Aggregate(E_1,E_1,H) = Aggregate(E_1,H) in semantic effect. Idempotency x\oplus x=x for semantically duplicate evidence.
rows.statement: Derives the first algebraic requirement, Idempotency x⊕x=x, from a duplicate-evidence thought experiment.

rows.anchor: 25C.5 — Experiment B: independent corroboration ... E_1 direct infrastructure query. E_2 independent backup-system query. Both support H. these should provide additional information. x\oplus y\neq x when x and y are genuinely independent information. Evidence identity and evidence independence are d
rows.statement: Shows independent (non-duplicate) evidence must genuinely increase support (x⊕y≠x), establishing Evidence identity and Evidence independence are different concepts.

rows.anchor: 25C.6 — Experiment C: dependent evidence ... E_1 Vendor documentation says X. E_2 Internal report copied from vendor documentation. E_2=f(E_1). Counting both as independent evidence creates false certainty. Therefore the algebra needs a dependency relation Dep(E_2,E_1). The effective independent inf
rows.statement: Requires an explicit Dep(E2,E1) dependency relation for copied evidence, reducing effective independent information to {E1} rather than {E1,E2}.

rows.anchor: 25C.7 — Experiment D: contradiction ... E_1\vdash H and E_2\vdash \neg H. A naive weighted average might produce Support(H)=0.5. But that loses critical information. The correct state is Conflict(H) with Support(H)>0 and Challenge(H)>0. Conflict\neq Uncertainty. This is extremely important. ... 25C.
rows.statement: Reaffirms Conflict≠Uncertainty via a three-case taxonomy (no evidence→Unknown; weak one-sided evidence→WeaklySupported; strong both-sided evidence→Conflicted), rejecting a naive weighted average that would collapse contradiction to 0.5.

rows.anchor: 25C.9 — Experiment E: stale evidence ... Was H true in 2024? it may be excellent. Is H true today? it may be insufficient. Support(E,H) must be evaluated relative to QuestionTime. We therefore need TemporalFit(E,H,t). ... 25C.10 — Experiment F: evidence reliability ... calibrated monitoring system v
rows.statement: Requires TemporalFit(E,H,t) for question-time-relative evidence assessment, and distinguishes Reliability from Relevance (a highly reliable source can still be irrelevant to a specific hypothesis).

rows.anchor: 25C.11 — Experiment G: authentic but false ... The backup is verified. The document is authentic. Later the actual restore test fails. Authenticity(E)=High while Support(H) may be reduced by stronger contradictory evidence. Authenticity\neq Correctness. This is another reason the dimensions must rem
rows.statement: Distinguishes Authenticity from Correctness — an authentic document can still turn out to be factually wrong upon later contradictory evidence.

rows.anchor: 25C.12 — Experiment H: AI evidence ... We cannot simply give it Reliability=0. That would also be too simplistic. An LLM can produce useful extraction; transformation; interpretation; hypothesis; hallucination. Therefore the system must represent how the AI output was produced. AIOutput \rightarrow
rows.statement: Argues AI-produced evidence should not automatically receive Reliability=0 (too simplistic); the system must represent AIOutput→Transformation→SourceArtifact, letting the underlying artifact carry the actual evidential weight.

rows.anchor: 25C.13 — Evidence provenance becomes part of aggregation ... E_1 from a source. E_2 is an LLM summary of E_1. E_3 is a human report based on E_2. Naively 3 pieces of evidence. Actually 1 underlying evidence lineage. Aggregation must operate over evidence lineage, not merely evidence count. This is a
rows.statement: States the major result that aggregation must operate over evidence lineage (a three-hop derivation chain collapses to one underlying lineage), not merely a count of records.

rows.anchor: 25C.14 — Algebraic requirement: commutativity ... E_1,E_2 versus E_2,E_1. The final semantic assessment should normally be identical. E_1\oplus E_2 = E_2\oplus E_1. Commutativity for order-independent evidence aggregation. If order matters, that must be explicitly because of temporal semantics, not
rows.statement: Derives the Commutativity requirement (E1⊕E2=E2⊕E1) for order-independent evidence aggregation, with order-dependence permitted only via explicit temporal semantics, never implementation accident.

rows.anchor: 25C.15 — Associativity ... (E_1\oplus E_2)\oplus E_3 = E_1\oplus(E_2\oplus E_3). This is associativity. If this fails, distributed computation becomes much harder. ... 25C.16 — But temporal evidence creates a qualification ... Aggregation may need to be evaluated relative to a query time. Aggregate(
rows.statement: Derives Associativity as a required property (needed for distributed computation), qualified by making aggregation contextual: Aggregate(E1,E2|QueryContext) with Time/Scope/Goal as context parameters.

rows.anchor: 25C.17 — First candidate structure ... \mathcal{E}(H)=(S_H,C_H,U_H,L_H) where supporting evidence lineage; challenging evidence lineage; unresolved/uncertain evidence; dependency/lineage structure. This is intentionally not yet a scalar score. ... 25C.18 — Why this is powerful ... Supported by two i
rows.statement: Defines a non-scalar aggregated evidence structure E(H)=(S_H,C_H,U_H,L_H) — supporting/challenging lineages, unresolved evidence, dependency structure — argued more epistemically useful than a bare confidence scalar.

rows.anchor: 25C.19 — But we eventually need numerical decisions ... Sārathi may need Risk(A_1)<Risk(A_2). Therefore numerical reasoning will eventually be required. But now we can make the correct architectural distinction: Evidence Algebra \rightarrow Assessment Representation \rightarrow Decision Model rather
rows.statement: Concedes numerical decision-making is eventually needed but insists on the layered architecture Evidence Algebra→Assessment Representation→Decision Model, never a direct Evidence→OneUniversalScore shortcut.

rows.anchor: 25C.20 — Candidate statistical layer ... P(H\mid E). Bayesian updating is attractive because it handles sequential evidence. But P(E_1,E_2\mid H) requires modeling dependencies. If we incorrectly assume P(E_1,E_2\mid H)=P(E_1\mid H)P(E_2\mid H), we may double-count correlated evidence. Therefore Bay
rows.statement: Evaluates Bayesian updating: attractive for sequential evidence, but naive conditional independence assumptions double-count correlated evidence — Bayesian math makes the dependency problem explicit rather than eliminating it.

rows.anchor: 25C.21 — Dempster–Shafer? ... Bel(H) and Pl(H). Bel(H)\neq Pl(H) can represent epistemic uncertainty without forcing a precise probability. But conflict handling and source dependence remain difficult. Candidate, not selected. ... 25C.22 — Fuzzy logic? ... \mu_H(x)\in[0,1] ... FuzzyMembership does n
rows.statement: Evaluates Dempster-Shafer (Bel≠Pl useful for uncertainty without forcing precision, but conflict/dependency handling remain difficult) and Fuzzy logic (FuzzyMembership≠Probability, useful for some domains but not universal) — both explicitly marked Candidate, not selected.

rows.anchor: 25C.23 — Weighted scoring? ... Score(H)=\sum_iw_i e_i. This is easy to compute. But it has severe problems: weights can be arbitrary; dependence is difficult; conflict can disappear into an average; calibration is unclear; 0.8 has no intrinsic epistemic meaning. Useful engineering heuristic\neq Univ
rows.statement: Evaluates weighted scoring, listing five severe problems (arbitrary weights, dependency difficulty, conflict disappearing into averages, unclear calibration, meaningless scalars) — a useful engineering heuristic, never a universal epistemic algebra.

rows.anchor: 25C.24 — The result of the comparison ... We therefore should not choose a single universal mathematical framework yet. Instead KnowledgeOS should probably have layers: Evidence Representation ↓ Evidence Dependency/Lineage ↓ Assessment Algebra ↓ Statistical/Logical Inference ↓ Decision Model. Differ
rows.statement: Consolidates the comparison result: no single universal framework is chosen; instead a five-layer architecture (Evidence Representation→Dependency/Lineage→Assessment Algebra→Statistical/Logical Inference→Decision Model) allows different bounded contexts to use different inference mechanisms.

rows.anchor: 25C.25 — A critical DDD insight ... We should not create a giant KnowledgeConfidenceService that decides everything. Evidence context knows Evidence and Provenance. Assessment context knows Support, Challenge, Reliability, Uncertainty. Statistical context knows Probability, Distribution, Calibration
rows.statement: Rejects a monolithic 'KnowledgeConfidenceService' in favor of four DDD bounded contexts (Evidence, Assessment, Statistical, Decision) each owning distinct concerns, communicating through explicit contracts.

rows.anchor: 25C.26 — Falsification test: order ... E_1,E_2,E_3 versus E_3,E_1,E_2. Expected Assessment_1=Assessment_2 provided the same temporal query context applies. If not, we have accidentally introduced processing-order dependence. ... 25C.27 — Falsification test: duplication ... E_1 versus E_1,E_1,E_1. Ex
rows.statement: Designs a falsification test for aggregation order-independence and a second test for exact-duplicate idempotency, explicitly flagging strengthened support from triple ingestion of the same evidence as a FAIL.

rows.anchor: 25C.28 — Falsification test: dependency ... E_1 versus E_1,E_2 where E_2=f(E_1). Expected EffectiveIndependentEvidence does not increase as if E_2 were independent. ... 25C.29 — Falsification test: contradiction ... E_1\vdash H, E_2\vdash\neg H. Expected Conflict(H)=True. Forbidden Confidence(H)=0.5
rows.statement: Designs a falsification test for dependent-evidence correction (EffectiveIndependentEvidence must not increase from a copy) and a contradiction test explicitly forbidding a naive Confidence=0.5 result without conflict information.

rows.anchor: 25C.30 — Falsification test: irrelevant evidence ... Add E_3 that has nothing to do with H. Expected Assessment(H,E_1,E_2,E_3) should be semantically equivalent to Assessment(H,E_1,E_2). Otherwise irrelevant information contaminates knowledge. ... 25C.31 — Falsification test: stale evidence ... Asse
rows.statement: Designs a falsification test requiring irrelevant evidence leave the assessment unchanged, and a staleness test proving assessment must be query-time-relative.

rows.anchor: 25C.32 — Falsification test: stronger evidence does not necessarily mean higher readiness ... E_1: RollbackUnknown. Then test E_2: RollbackFailed. Evidence quality has improved. But Readiness can decrease. EvidenceStrength\neq GoalUtility. This separation must remain in the architecture.
rows.statement: Designs a falsification test reaffirming EvidenceStrength ≠ GoalUtility (improved evidence quality can decrease readiness), a separation that must remain architectural.

rows.anchor: 25C.33 — We have now found the likely shape of the algebra ... \mathcal{A}(H\mid C,t) as the assessment state of hypothesis H under context C and evaluation time t. It contains \mathcal{A}=(Support,Challenge,Uncertainty,Dependency,TemporalFit,Provenance). Then a separate inference function may map t
rows.statement: Consolidates the likely algebra shape: assessment state A(H|C,t)=(Support,Challenge,Uncertainty,Dependency,TemporalFit,Provenance) with a separate Inference(A,M)→Result function parameterized by the chosen mathematical model M — cleaner than treating assessment itself as a probability.

rows.anchor: 25C.34 — A crucial distinction emerges ... Layer 1 — Evidence state \mathcal{E} "What information do we have?" sources.note: The actual executed results of the KR-SIM-2026-09-02 simulation experiment mandated by this batch's own v1.1 simulation protocol (S2379): all 10 scenario families (A-J) execute the full epistemic lifecycle and 19 of 20 properties hold, but P11 (factivity) fails NECESSARILY -- a genuine negative structural theorem (not a bug) proving DEF-1 factivity (Knows(a,p,c,t)->True(p,c,t)) and the v1.1 attribution equation K=Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) are jointly unsatisfiable for any total Gamma that attributes anything, since Gamma is a function of E alone and E contains no truth (demonstrated by a bit-identical-epistemic-state witness across two worlds with different ground truth, and confirmed at a 0.1237 conditional failure rate over 10,000 randomized trials). Also finds Adequate and Zero are extensionally identical (both reduce to Delta_t=empty, so DEF-20 does no independent work of DEF-22), semantic equivalence remains circular, and Revision-without-retraction produces permanent underdetermination in any world that changes over time (the theory's single Revise operation cannot express the corpus's seven revision verbs). A 26-type formal type table finds 10 notation collisions (worst: P three-way Proposition/Probability/Preservation-vector; E dangerously conflates Evidence and the new v1.1 EpistemicState) but zero genuine type collisions. A no-smuggling audit finds oracle independence clean (World.truth unreadable by any agent transition, the load-bearing guarantee making the factivity result real rather than an artifact) but flags one instrumentation artifact (three scenarios construct observation tokens directly rather than through a channel) and two open unauditable questions (hypothesis-space narrowing, requirement-kind exhaustiveness).

rows.anchor: **`[EXP]` The theory is executable and its distinctions survive — with one exception, and the exception is structural rather than incidental.** All 10 scenario families (A–J) execute the full lifecycle. 19 of 20 properties hold across the deterministic suite. **`P11` (factivity) fails, and it fails necessarily.**
rows.statement: States the overall simulation result: the theory is executable and its distinctions survive across all 10 scenario families and 19 of 20 tested properties, with the single exception of P11 (factivity), which fails not incidentally but necessarily -- a structural finding, not a bug.

rows.anchor: (1) Knows(a,p,c,t) -> True(p,c,t) DEF-1, factivity (2) K_{a,c,t} = Gamma(E_{a,c,t}, Q_t, C_t, EC_t) v1.1 attribution ... **These are jointly unsatisfiable for any total `Γ` that attributes anything.** Witness: two worlds whose truths differ ... produce a **bit-identical epistemic state** ... Since Γ is a function of E, it returns an identical K. The attribution is true in one world and false in the other.
rows.statement: Proves by explicit witness that v1.0's DEF-1 factivity (Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t)) and the v1.1 attribution equation K=Gamma(E,Q,C,EC) are jointly unsatisfiable for any total Gamma that attributes anything: two worlds with different ground truth (os=RHEL9.8 vs RHEL8.6) produce a bit-identical epistemic state E (verified by fingerprint over observations/evidence/interpretations/assessments/determinations/hypotheses/rejections), so any function of E alone must return the identical attribution K regardless of which world is actually true -- Gamma's domain structurally excludes truth.

rows.anchor: Policy sweep — the only `Γ` that escapes is the one that attributes nothing: justified-unique yes/yes, justified-any yes/yes, none no/no. Randomized confirmation over 10 000 trials: **420 factivity violations**, conditional failure rate **0.1237** given that an attribution was made. Diagnosis: **414 / 665** violations when a source the admission policy rated reliable reported a false value, **0 / 2 607** otherwise.
rows.statement: Confirms the factivity impossibility across every tested attribution policy (justified-unique and justified-any both violate factivity whenever they attribute anything; only the trivial policy 'attribute nothing' escapes), and via a 10,000-trial randomized run: 420 factivity violations, a 0.1237 conditional failure rate given an attribution was made, with the failure concentrated entirely (414 of 665, vs 0 of 2,607) in cases where a policy-trusted reliable source reported a false value that the agent had no signal to distinguish from a true one.

rows.anchor: S3 anti-fabrication ... S4 unresolved competition ... S5 target-relative assessment ... S6 evidence dependence ... S7/S8 explicit standards & models ... S10 inquiry-relative adequacy ... S11 history ... S14 no information creation ... S15 decision lane ... S17 unknown taxonomy
rows.statement: Confirms ten major theory-level successes against the protocol's success criteria: anti-fabrication (incomplete evidence never invents a value), unresolved competition (Reject(H1) never becomes Accept(H2), determination stays set-valued), target-relative evidence weighting (never a bare scalar strength), correct evidence dependence handling (dependence-aware run drops a duplicate that the naive run double-counts), standards and models producing genuinely different determinations from identical evidence/reality, inquiry-relative adequacy (same K_t, different I_t/Delta_t/Zero across two inquiries), history preservation (K_1!=K_2 with stable identity and recoverable K_1), no unsupported information creation (an injected unsupported conclusion is caught), a fully separable four-stage decision lane (Determination->Proposal->Decision->Authorization->Action), and a non-collapsing four-way unknown taxonomy.

rows.anchor: **What object is `K_t`, if it cannot be factive?** ... **`Adequate` and `Zero` are extensionally identical** — `DEF-20` and `DEF-22` both reduce to Delta_t = empty. One does no independent work. ... **Semantic equivalence remains circular** ... **Revision without retraction produces permanent underdetermination**
rows.statement: Names four major unresolved questions the experiment surfaced: what K_t even is if it cannot be factive; DEF-20 (Adequate) and DEF-22 (Zero) are extensionally identical (both reduce to Delta_t=empty), meaning one definition does no independent work; semantic equivalence remains circular since behaviour is compared only under an experimenter-chosen projection; and Revision without retraction produces permanent underdetermination since the theory models only one of the corpus's seven revision verbs.

rows.anchor: The factivity result is the first genuinely **negative structural theorem** the programme has produced about its own definitions, and it is *sharp*: it does not say the theory is wrong, it says **exactly two of its clauses cannot both hold**, and it names the three repairs available
rows.statement: Names the factivity finding the programme's first genuinely negative structural theorem about its own definitions: sharp in that it does not claim the theory is wrong overall, only that exactly two specific clauses (DEF-1 factivity and the v1.1 attribution equation) cannot both hold, with three named repairs available elsewhere in the artifact set.

rows.anchor: `definitional = true` marks a property whose oracle necessarily restates a theory definition: its pass is a **logical consequence of the implementation**, not independent evidence. ... P3 Rejection != Acceptance **yes** -- Reject removes one member by construction. P4 Gap != Zero ... **yes** -- Zero := (Delta=empty) is DEF-22.
rows.statement: Establishes a definitional-vs-independent classification discipline for every tested property, flagging P3 (Rejection != Acceptance, true by construction since Reject removes one member) and P4 (Gap != Zero, true by definition since DEF-22 literally defines Zero as Delta=empty) as definitional -- their passing is a logical consequence of the implementation, never independent evidence that the theory works.

rows.anchor: **P11** Knowledge attribution respects factivity Knows(a,p,c,t) -> True(p,c,t) **no — the only fully oracle-independent property** ... Only **P11** is fully oracle-independent: its evaluator reads World.truth, which no agent transition can access (verified by static audit). Every other property compares the agent's state against itself under a definition supplied by the theory.
rows.statement: Identifies P11 (factivity) as the ONLY fully oracle-independent property among all 20 tested: its evaluator reads World.truth, structurally inaccessible to any agent transition, whereas every other property merely compares the agent's own state against itself under a theory-supplied definition -- explaining why P11's failure carries far more evidentiary weight than any pass among the other 19.

rows.anchor: `P7` is marked non-definitional but is **partly circular** — see `I-circularity-register.md` CIRC-5.
rows.statement: Flags P7 (representation equality is not required for semantic equality) as partly circular despite being marked non-definitional, cross-referencing an unread-in-this-batch circularity register entry CIRC-5.

rows.anchor: A Simple determination ... K is a *record with status, provenance, weight* — **not a copy of the observation**. B Incomplete evidence ... status=cannot-determine, A=empty, Zero=false, Delta!=empty, **nothing invented**. C Competing hypotheses ... A={RHEL9.8,RHEL8.6} underdetermined ... Reject(H1) did **not** become Accept(H2).
rows.statement: Reports scenarios A-C executed results: A confirms Knowledge is a structured record (status/provenance/weight), not a copy of observation; B confirms incomplete evidence produces cannot-determine/empty-A/Zero-false/non-empty-Gap with nothing invented; C confirms Reject(H1) does not become Accept(H2), leaving the determination genuinely underdetermined between two surviving hypotheses.

rows.anchor: D Different standards ... S-lenient -> **unique**; S-strict (corroboration) -> **cannot-determine**. Evidence and truth verified byte-identical across arms. ... E Different inquiries ... same K_t; I_1!=I_2; Delta_1=empty, Delta_2={r2}; Zero_1=true, Zero_2=false.
rows.statement: Reports scenario D (holding evidence and truth byte-identical while varying only the epistemic standard S^epi flips the determination from unique to cannot-determine, confirming standards do real work) and scenario E (a fixed E_t under two different inquiries produces identical K_t but different Ideal States, Gaps, and Zero values, confirming inquiry-relative adequacy).

rows.anchor: F Conflicting evidence ... A={8081,8082} underdetermined — **not averaged**, conflict preserved, no attribution. G Dependent evidence ... dependence-aware: 1 assessment dropped ... corroboration requirement unmet. Naive: counts both. H Model mismatch ... M1: beta=1.852, R2=0.899, causal_status = not-identified; true effect 0. **No causal knowledge attributed**.
rows.statement: Reports scenario F (conflicting equal-reliability evidence is preserved as conflict, never averaged, and produces no attribution), G (a dependence-aware run correctly drops a derived duplicate and finds the corroboration requirement unmet, while a naive run incorrectly double-counts it), and H (a confounded model with excellent statistical fit, R^2=0.899, is correctly classified causal_status=not-identified against a true zero causal effect, so no causal knowledge is attributed despite the fit).

rows.anchor: I Retrospective revision ... K_1!=K_2, identity stable, pre-revision determination stored in history. J Unobservable property ... classified **UNOBSERVABLE** — not observed-false, not probability zero, not a rejected hypothesis.
rows.statement: Reports scenario I (reality change plus revision produces K_1!=K_2 with stable identity and the pre-revision determination preserved in history) and J (a property with no channel at all is correctly classified UNOBSERVABLE, never conflated with observed-false, probability-zero, or a rejected hypothesis).

rows.anchor: UNOBSERVED a channel exists, never queried ... UNINTERPRETED observation held, no semantic content assigned ... UNDERDETERMINED evidence present, |A_t|>1 ... UNOBSERVABLE no channel exists ... P13 confirms UNOBSERVABLE != UNDERDETERMINED in both the deterministic and randomized layers (guard active in 37.4% of 10 000 trials, 0 failures).
rows.statement: Confirms the four-way unknown taxonomy (Unobserved: channel exists but never queried; Uninterpreted: observation held with no assigned semantic content; Underdetermined: evidence present with |A_t|>1; Unobservable: no channel exists) did not collapse across both deterministic scenarios and the randomized layer, with P13 (Unobservable!=Underdetermined) confirmed active in 37.4% of 10,000 randomized trials with zero failures.

rows.anchor: D is the only scenario that holds **reality, observation, evidence and inquiry fixed** and varies a single theory object. It therefore isolates `S^epi` cleanly, and it is the one place the experiment shows an epistemic standard doing real work rather than decorating the model.
rows.statement: Identifies Scenario D as the methodologically strongest of the ten scenarios: the only one holding reality, observation, evidence, AND inquiry all fixed while varying a single theory object (S^epi), cleanly isolating epistemic standards and showing them doing real work rather than merely decorating the model.

rows.statement: Finds ten notation collisions across the v1.0/v1.1 theory's symbol vocabulary (worst: P used three ways for Proposition, Probability, and the Preservation vector), and flags the E collision as the most DANGEROUS: the v1.1 correction reuses E for EpistemicState while DEF-7 already uses E for Evidence -- precisely the two objects the v1.1 correction's entire point is to keep from being confused, an ironic self-undermining notation clash.

rows.anchor: **1. Instance-level, not reachability-level.** The prior lane (`KR-2026-09-01`) reasoned about *which carrier kinds are reachable*; its own `THM-9` then established `Reachability ≠ Adequacy`. This simulator therefore carries **content**: tokens, readings, weights, sources, provenance. Only that makes factivity, dependence, ambiguity and fabrication testable at all.
rows.statement: States the first of two design decisions making the v1.1 simulation's results meaningful: unlike the prior KR-2026-09-01 kernel-reduction lane (which reasoned only about reachability of carrier kinds, whose own THM-9 established Reachability != Adequacy), this simulator carries actual instance-level CONTENT (tokens, readings, weights, sources, provenance) -- only this design choice makes factivity, dependence, ambiguity and fabrication testable at all.

rows.anchor: **2. Oracle independence is enforced structurally.** `World.truth` is read by the **evaluator only**. A static audit greps every agent-side module for `.truth` and reports any hit as smuggling. Result: **zero hits**. This is what makes `P11` an empirical test rather than a definition — and, as it turns out, it is also *why* factivity fails.
rows.statement: States the second design decision: oracle independence is enforced STRUCTURALLY, not by convention -- World.truth is read only by the evaluator, verified by a static audit greping every agent-side module for any access, with zero hits found -- this structural guarantee is precisely what makes P11 (factivity) an empirical test rather than a mere definitional restatement, and is also directly why factivity was found to fail (the agent genuinely has no path to truth).

rows.anchor: a lexicon maps tokens to admissible readings, context-indexed | Interpret | ambiguity handling changes ... an admission policy assigns per-source reliability | Qualify | the factivity failure rate changes; the *possibility* does not ... dependence is declared via `derived_from`, not inferred | Qualify | G/P8 becomes untestable if removed
rows.statement: Declares five explicit model assumptions per the protocol's mandatory-assumption-declaration discipline: a context-indexed lexicon (affecting ambiguity handling), a per-source reliability admission policy (affecting the factivity failure RATE but not its possibility), a threshold-plus-corroboration standard, weight-maximizing tie-breaking in Determine, and declared (not inferred) evidence dependence via derived_from -- each with its consequence if changed stated explicitly.

rows.anchor: SMUG-0 -- Oracle independence: **CLEAN** ... forbidden_reads : NONE. No agent transition can read latent truth. This is the load-bearing guarantee of the whole experiment — and it is precisely what makes CE-1 a real result rather than an artifact.
rows.statement: Confirms SMUG-0: a static audit of every agent-side module finds zero reads of World.truth -- no agent transition can access latent truth, explicitly named the load-bearing guarantee of the whole experiment and precisely what makes CE-1 (the factivity counterexample) a real theory result rather than a simulator artifact.

rows.statement: Finds SMUG-1: scenarios C, F and G construct their observation tokens directly after Acquire rather than having the world produce them through a channel, classified as an instrumentation artifact (not capability smuggling, since the overridden value is a legitimate scenario input) but explicitly noting these three scenarios therefore do NOT actually exercise the acquisition channel and that claim must never be made of them; recommends dedicated fixed-token channels for the next run.

rows.statement: Verifies SMUG-2: each of nine semantic capabilities (world-contact, evidential admission, meaning assignment, hypothesis space, target-relative weight, set-valued selection, elimination, attribution, state commit) is introduced by exactly one named transition, with the lexicon and admission policy correctly classified as declared inputs/data (recorded in provenance as assumptions), not capabilities -- a different lexicon changes readings but cannot create a capability no transition owns.

rows.statement: Records CE-3: after reality changes and new evidence arrives, the t0 assessment is never retracted and still carries full weight, so the determination becomes permanently underdetermined ({RHEL9.8, RHEL8.6}) rather than reflecting the new reality; root cause is that DEF-23/AX-4 give the theory only Revise, while the corpus carries seven distinct revision verbs (Update, Revise, Supersede, Correct, Invalidate, Retract, Expire) of which only one is modelled -- classified THEORY GAP (not an implementation bug, since the implementation does exactly what the theory specifies), meaning any world that changes over time drives the agent monotonically toward underdetermination; notes P19 (identity-preservation) still passes, so a narrower test would have entirely missed this failure mode; ties directly to the pre-existing open question Q-4 about whether the seven revision verbs are epistemically distinguishable, now with a concrete failing case attached.

Only **P11** is fully oracle-independent: its evaluator reads World.truth, which no agent transition can access (verified by static audit). Every other property compares the agent's state against itself under a definition supplied by the theory.
rationale_evidence.statement: Identifies P11 (factivity) as the ONLY fully oracle-independent property among all 20 tested: its evaluator reads World.truth, structurally inaccessible to any agent transition, whereas every other property merely compares the agent's own state against itself under a theory-supplied definition -- explaining why P11's failure carries far more evidentiary weight than any pass among the other 19.

rationale_evidence.anchor: D is the only scenario that holds **reality, observation, evidence and inquiry fixed** and varies a single theory object. It therefore isolates `S^epi` cleanly, and it is the one place the experiment shows an epistemic standard doing real work rather than decorating the model.
rationale_evidence.statement: Identifies Scenario D as the methodologically strongest of the ten scenarios: the only one holding reality, observation, evidence, AND inquiry all fixed while varying a single theory object (S^epi), cleanly isolating epistemic standards and showing them doing real work rather than merely decorating the model.

rationale_evidence.anchor: **1. Instance-level, not reachability-level.** The prior lane (`KR-2026-09-01`) reasoned about *which carrier kinds are reachable*; its own `THM-9` then established `Reachability ≠ Adequacy`. This simulator therefore carries **content**: tokens, readings, weights, sources, provenance. Only that makes factivity, dependence, ambiguity and fabrication testable at all.
rationale_evidence.statement: States the first of two design decisions making the v1.1 simulation's results meaningful: unlike the prior KR-2026-09-01 kernel-reduction lane (which reasoned only about reachability of carrier kinds, whose own THM-9 established Reachability != Adequacy), this simulator carries actual instance-level CONTENT (tokens, readings, weights, sources, provenance) -- only this design choice makes factivity, dependence, ambiguity and fabrication testable at all.

rationale_evidence.anchor: **2. Oracle independence is enforced structurally.** `World.truth` is read by the **evaluator only**. A static audit greps every agent-side module for `.truth` and reports any hit as smuggling. Result: **zero hits**. This is what makes `P11` an empirical test rather than a definition — and, as it turns out, it is also *why* factivity fails.
rationale_evidence.statement: States the second design decision: oracle independence is enforced STRUCTURALLY, not by convention -- World.truth is read only by the evaluator, verified by a static audit greping every agent-side module for any access, with zero hits found -- this structural guarantee is precisely what makes P11 (factivity) an empirical test rather than a mere definitional restatement, and is also directly why factivity was found to fail (the agent genuinely has no path to truth).

aliases: Epistemic Error, Refutation, Retraction, Correction and Revision

sources.note: S0905's Step 25M: the six-way RevisionType taxonomy and revision-as-event-addition model, extending S0903's closure/state-machine invariants and S0904's distributed-retraction discussion into a full non-monotonic-knowledge treatment.

rows.anchor: K_{t+1}=Revise(K_t,E_{new}) ... H_{t+1}\supseteq H_t ... current state may change without destroying the history
rows.statement: Restates the revision model K_{t+1}=Revise(K_t,E_new) alongside additive history H_{t+1}⊇H_t, so current state can change without destroying its historical derivation.

rows.anchor: RevisionType=\{Evolution,Correction,Retraction,Refutation,Reinterpretation,ModelRevision\}
rows.statement: Introduces a six-value RevisionType taxonomy for 'something previously accepted is later discovered to be wrong': Evolution, Correction, Retraction, Refutation, Reinterpretation, ModelRevision — argued to require distinct treatment since collapsing them into one Boolean 'wrong' loses epistemic information; recommended as part of the domain language.

rows.anchor: A_1\rightarrow A_2 if an actual upgrade occurred ... Evolution\neq Correction. The old knowledge remains historically valid
rows.statement: Defines Evolution: a genuine world state change (A1 at t1 -> A2 at t2) where the first assertion was true when made — Evolution ≠ Correction, old knowledge remains historically valid.

rows.anchor: Correction(E_1,E_2) ... Status(E_1)=Corrected ... a new event rather than a destructive modification
rows.statement: Defines Correction: a source reporting its own earlier record was a typo/error is represented as Correction(E1,E2) with Status(E1)=Corrected, the original event remaining in history as a new event rather than a destructive modification.

rows.anchor: Support(A)\downarrow but does not necessarily establish \neg A ... Retraction\neq Refutation ... especially important for statistical reasoning
rows.statement: Defines Retraction: a source withdrawing support lowers Support(A) but does not establish ¬A — Retraction ≠ Refutation, 'losing support for a hypothesis is not automatically equivalent to proving the hypothesis false' — 'especially important for statistical reasoning.'

rows.anchor: A\perp B ... if new evidence is sufficiently authoritative, A may be classified as Refuted ... refutation is a conclusion derived from evidence and domain semantics; it is not merely the existence of a second assertion
rows.statement: Defines Refutation: when a domain model treats two same-context/time assertions as mutually exclusive (A⊥B) and new evidence is sufficiently authoritative, A may be classified Refuted — a conclusion derived from evidence plus domain semantics, not merely a second assertion existing.

rows.anchor: command was actually executed against the development system ... ObservationValid\land AssertionInvalid ... exactly why the layered model from 25I is necessary
rows.statement: Defines Reinterpretation: an observation can remain valid while the derived assertion is wrong (e.g. a command result correctly observed but wrongly attributed to production instead of development) — ObservationValid ∧ AssertionInvalid — explicitly validating the necessity of S0901's layered Observation/Representation/Assertion model.

rows.anchor: HasIP(Server,x) is functional ... Later we correct the domain model ... \Omega_1\rightarrow\Omega_2 ... K^{\Omega_1}\neq K^{\Omega_2} ... ModelRevision ... historical interpretation under \Omega_1 must remain reproducible
rows.statement: Defines ModelRevision using the IP-address-functionality example: the underlying observations are unchanged but a domain-model correction (Omega1->Omega2) changes the interpretation (K^Omega1 ≠ K^Omega2); the historical Omega1-based interpretation must remain reproducible.

lineage_claims.quote: Under that model, two IP addresses constitute a conflict. Later we correct the domain model...

rows.anchor: K^{(1)}=Derive(H,\Omega_1) and K^{(2)}=Derive(H,\Omega_2) ... Interpretation is versioned
rows.statement: States KnowledgeOS should answer both 'what did the system conclude under model version 1.0?' and '...under model version 2.0?' via K^(1)=Derive(H,Omega1), K^(2)=Derive(H,Omega2) — 'Interpretation is versioned.'

rows.anchor: H'=H\cup\{E_{revision}\} ... K'=Derive(H',\Omega,EC,M) ... Revision=EventAddition+StateReDerivation ... considerably cleaner than destructive updates
rows.statement: Formalizes revision as operating through the event history rather than direct mutation: H'=H∪{E_revision}, K'=Derive(H',Omega,EC,M) — Revision = EventAddition + StateReDerivation, 'considerably cleaner than destructive updates.'

rows.anchor: E_1:Nexus=3.70 followed by E_2:Correction(E_1,3.69) ... K_{current}=3.69 ... can still reconstruct K_{before correction}=3.70 ... nothing historically meaningful has been erased
rows.statement: Worked example: after a correction event, the system derives current state 3.69 while still being able to reconstruct the pre-correction state 3.70 — 'nothing historically meaningful has been erased.'

rows.anchor: Assessment(A): Strong\rightarrow Weak ... Assertion\neq Assessment
rows.statement: Worked example: discovering an unreliable measurement method changes an assertion's support Assessment (Strong->Weak) without refuting the proposition itself — Assertion ≠ Assessment, flagged as important for the upcoming formal evidence-aggregation step.

rows.anchor: P(H\mid E_1)=0.95 ... P(H\mid E_1,E_2)=0.40 ... has not logically been proven false ... Probability revision\neq Logical refutation ... must not invent priors or probability models implicitly
rows.statement: Worked numerical example (P(H|E1)=0.95 dropping to P(H|E1,E2)=0.40) shows substantially reduced support without logical refutation — Probability revision ≠ Logical refutation; permits Bayesian updating P(H|E1,E2) ∝ P(E2|H,E1)P(H|E1) where an explicit probabilistic model exists, but warns the system must not implicitly invent priors or probability models.

rows.anchor: ValidFrom\le t<ValidUntil ... KnowledgeOS must support both DeterministicModels and ProbabilisticModels ... should not reduce the entire KnowledgeState to a probability distribution
rows.statement: Reaffirms deterministic and probabilistic knowledge coexist (e.g. validity-interval evaluation needs no probability) — KnowledgeOS must support both, not reduce everything to a probability distribution.

rows.anchor: Evidence E1->Assertion A1->Knowledge K1->Requirement R1->Zero->Lord->Decision D1 ... Revision propagation=Support recomputation, not cascading deletion
rows.statement: Worked dependency-chain example: retracting E1 must propagate through Assertion->Knowledge->Requirement->Zero->Lord->Decision without deleting downstream state; if A1 also has independent support E2, retracting E1 may weaken but not destroy A1 — 'Revision propagation = Support recomputation, not cascading deletion.'

rows.anchor: RF(E) ... Recalculate(RF(E)) ... an incremental computation strategy rather than requiring the entire knowledge graph to be rebuilt
rows.statement: Defines the Affected Revision Frontier RF(E) as the set of knowledge objects potentially affected by a revision event, enabling incremental recomputation (Recalculate(RF(E))) instead of full-graph rebuilds.

rows.anchor: change in NexusVersion affects migration/compatibility/patch compliance ... no reason to invalidate unrelated knowledge such as employee onboarding ... Revision propagation follows semantic dependencies
rows.statement: Bounds revision propagation by semantic dependency (a version change affects migration/compatibility/patch-compliance knowledge but not unrelated domains like employee onboarding), mapped in DDD terms to explicit cross-bounded-context integration relationships rather than an uncontrolled global dependency graph.

rows.anchor: Zero=\varnothing ... Later, supporting evidence is invalidated ... Zero\neq\varnothing ... Zero is dynamic
rows.statement: Derives a property of Zero under revision: a previously-satisfied requirement (Zero=∅) can reopen (Zero≠∅) when supporting evidence is later invalidated — 'Zero is dynamic,' representing the current epistemic gap, not a permanent requirement characteristic.

rows.anchor: D_1=Migrate ... evidence supporting a prerequisite is invalidated ... DecisionAffected(D_1)=True ... should not automatically reverse the decision unless the applicable governance policy explicitly permits
rows.statement: A prior decision (e.g. Migrate) whose supporting evidence is later invalidated becomes DecisionAffected=True, but automatic reversal requires explicit governance permission — the system may instead require review/pause/revocation/reassessment/no-action, 'preserving the distinction between computation and authority.'

rows.anchor: \{Valid,Superseded,Questioned,Invalidated,Executed,Reversed\} ... Historical existence\neq Current validity
rows.statement: Defines a six-value decision-status lifecycle {Valid, Superseded, Questioned, Invalidated, Executed, Reversed}; historical decisions remain historical even if later invalidated — 'Historical existence ≠ Current validity.'

rows.anchor: Seven revision falsification tests (genuine evolution; wrong target/reinterpretation; source withdrawal; genuine refutation; model revision; redundant support; decision dependency) — all PASS
rows.statement: Runs seven worked falsification tests against the revision model, all recorded PASS: (1) genuine time-ordered version change classified Evolution, not error; (2) an observation correctly made against the wrong target yields Observation=Valid, Assertion=Invalid; (3) a source's withdrawal yields EvidenceStatus=Retracted, not automatically Assertion=False; (4) two mutually-exclusive same-scope assertions with authoritative new evidence yield OtherAssertion=Refuted; (5) an ontology-model change (Omega1->Omega2) yields SameHistory with potentially DifferentDerivedKnowledge; (6) an assertion supported by two independent evidence items remains supported after retracting one, via the other; (7) retracting evidence feeding a decision yields DecisionAffected=True with automatic reversal remaining governed rather than assumed.

experiment.hypothesis: The six-way RevisionType taxonomy and its associated invariants (event-addition, support-recomputation, governed decision reversal) behave correctly across seven distinct revision scenarios.
experiment.setup: Seven scenarios: genuine evolution; wrong-target observation; source withdrawal; genuine refutation; model revision; redundant/independent support; decision dependency chain.
experiment.method: apply the revision model's classification and propagation rules to each scenario
experiment.result: All seven scenarios produce the theoretically expected classification/state
experiment.interpretation: Confirms the revision taxonomy and propagation rules are internally consistent across the tested cases.
experiment.limitations: illustrative, not executed against real data

rows.anchor: EventAppend, DependencyTraversal, SupportRecalculation, TemporalEvaluation, RuleEvaluation, StateReconstruction ... a normal PC can perform these operations ... a scalability concern rather than a theoretical obstacle
rows.statement: Lists the revision model's core operations (EventAppend, DependencyTraversal, SupportRecalculation, TemporalEvaluation, RuleEvaluation, StateReconstruction) as ordinary, normal-PC computable; large-scale needs (incremental computation, dependency indexes, caching, materialized views) are a scalability, not theoretical, concern.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS must be able to revise its current epistemic state without destroying the historical events that explain how the earlier state arose ... H_{t+1}=H_t\cup\{RevisionEvent\} ... K_{t+1}=Derive(H_{t+1},\Omega,EC,M)
rows.statement: States the central 25M invariant: revision of current epistemic state must never destroy the historical events explaining how the earlier state arose, formalized as H_{t+1}=H_t∪{RevisionEvent}, K_{t+1}=Derive(H_{t+1},Omega,EC,M).

rows.anchor: 25M — PASS ... World Change, Knowledge Change, Assessment Change, Model Change ... related, but they are not the same event
rows.statement: Step 25M self-verdict: PASS, with the central result that the model now distinguishes four fundamentally different dimensions — World Change, Knowledge Change, Assessment Change, Model Change — related but not the same event, 'substantially strengthens the KnowledgeOS epistemic model.'

Confidence=Average(SourceConfidences) ... statistically unjustified in the general case ... Confidence
eq Probability
eq Reliability
eq Authority
eq Support
eq Independence
rows.statement: Closes by reiterating the deliberately-avoided naive confidence-averaging rule and posing the precise next question — how KnowledgeOS should aggregate heterogeneous evidence (independent/duplicate/derived/correlated/contradictory/authoritative/stale/retracted) without statistical double-counting — transitioning to Step 25N (Evidence Aggregation Algebra), which will separate six terms: Confidence, Probability, Reliability, Authority, Support, Independence.
